Allow an operator to set a rbd_data_pool

In order to be able to consume an Erasure Coding data pool,
rbd_data_pool must be set to the configured Erasing coding pool
along with the standard rbd replicated pool.

revisions.message:
Pass volume summary filters from API to DB layer

The volume summary API accepts volume filters but they
are not applied when calling down to the database layer.

This fixes that bug by passing the filters.

Closes-Bug: #2080228
Change-Id: I9efee1a14d670c193768ffef67b1b24e635a6d86

Pass volume summary filters from API to DB layer

The volume summary API accepts volume filters but they
are not applied when calling down to the database layer.

This fixes that bug by passing the filters. This also
fixes the bug where we would throw a 500 instead of 400
error when passing invalid parameters to this API.

Depends-On: https://review.opendev.org/c/openstack/openstacksdk/+/928867

Dell PowerScale: Added support of revert to snapshot

This change adds revert-to-snapshot support to the Dell PowerScale
Manila driver. When revert_to_snapshot_support is enabled in the share
type, the driver creates a Domain Mark job during share creation and
uses asynchronous SnapRevert jobs for the actual revert operation.

The driver returns STATUS_REVERTING_TO_SNAPSHOT and relies on the
periodic task in the share manager (from the core change) to poll
the backend job status via get_share_status.

Configuration options:
- powerscale_job_retries: Max polling attempts (default: 5)
- powerscale_job_interval: Polling interval in seconds (default: 2)

Build container images on Debian Trixie

This updates the base platform for Zuul's container images from Debian
Bookworm to Trixie. The python version remains fixed at python3.11 for
now, but we'll get updated system tools like git.

As part of this change support for very old debuntu versions within the
bindep.txt file is cleaned up to simplify the ruleset. We also
temporarily fetch dependencies from docker hub while we wait for opendev
to mirror them for us.

revisions.message:
Add Weblate support to translation update pipeline

This patch introduces Weblate support alongside the existing Zanata
workflow as part of the translation infrastructure migration. Both
systems will run in parallel during the transition period to ensure
smooth migration from Zanata to Weblate.

Changes include:
- Add weblate_api_credentials to propose-translation-update job
- Add prepare-weblate-client role to translation playbook
- Add Weblate translation update script execution

The Weblate script runs with WEBLATE_URL and WEBLATE_TOKEN
environment variables provided by the weblate_api_credentials secret.
This allows testing Weblate functionality while maintaining the
existing Zanata workflow.

During the transition period:
- Zanata script handles existing translations (may result in no changes)
- Weblate script processes new translations from migrated projects
- Both scripts can run without conflicts

Once Weblate migration is validated,
the Zanata components will be removed in a follow-up patch.

branch to the master branch.

branches and catch performance issues earlier.

revisions.message:
Support deploy amphora in different availability zones

- Added option to enable multizone deployment in Octavia config
  Enabling this option changes behaviour for creation Amphora in
  availability zones (more detailes below).
- Added attribute for octavia availability zones, which indicates, that
  AZ could be used in multizone deployment.
- Added attribute for amphora resource to indicate, which AZ was
  calculated in multizone deployment.
- Added validation to create Loadbalancer with multizone enabled flag,
  but without configured AZ. It's not allowed to do.
- Main logic is placed in ComputeCreate task.

Key ideas:

  availability zones (more detailes below).

  AZ could be used in multizone deployment.

  calculated in multizone deployment.

  but without configured AZ. It's not allowed to do.
- Main logic is placed in ComputeCreate task.

Key ideas:
- Now Octavia AZ could be marked as available for multizone usage.
- After enabling multizone in config marked octavia AZ will be used for
  creation amphora desributed in these AZs.
- If NO AZ available (marked for multizone), the default config option
  will be used.
  It's done for compatible with non multizone mode.
- If multizone mode enabled and availability zone is specified on API
  request directly - it will ignore multizone logic and creates all
  amphora in the same target AZ. Also it will continue work in the same
  way in failover, i.e. amphora will be re-created in the same AZ.
  It's done for compatible with non multizone mode.
- AZ should have "compute_zone" and "volume_zone" to be marked as
  available for multizone deployment.

Important: Octavia with with the same compute_zone handled as one AZ,
because administrator could configure several AZ like:
az1:        compute_zone - Z1, volume_zone - Z1
az1_extra:  compute_zone - Z1, volume_zone - Z1_extra

And in this case will be incorrect to desctribute Amphoras in the same
compute AZ, because we want to provide different AZ for compute zones
firstly.

In deployment with enabled multizone AZ for amphora will be calculated
on creation Loadbalancer and on Failover LB/Amphora. The logic is
following:
- Group octavia AZs by uniq compute zones.
- Find AZ index for master/single amphora by loadbalancer id hash like:
  idx = hash(lb_id) % len(uniq_compute_zones)
- Get compute AZ from group on first step. Take first octavia AZ
  associated with this compute AZ - it will be a AZ for master/single
  amphora.
- For Backup amphora use random octavia AZ, exclude octavia AZs with the
  same compute_zone as for Master amphora.
  If there no such AZs - the same AZ as for Master amphora will be used.

OR if AZ is already specified for amphora:
- take AZ fro amphora and check, that this AZ is enabled and marked for
  multizone.
- if it's true - use this AZ
- otherwise re-calculate AZ. BUT do not update AZ in amphora
  description, to allow creation amphora in "correct" zone after turning
  this AZ back.

Deploy Kerbside with Kolla-Ansible.

This change implements the Kerbside Kolla-Ansible deployment role. It is a
fairly large change, but I couldn't find a meaningful way to break it up
into smaller chunks.

The basic idea is that there is a proxy sitting in front of the Nova
hypervisors that can talk the SPICE protocol to clients, lookup where the
console is on the relevant hypervisor, and then build a SPICE connection
to that hypervisor. It then shovels SPICE packets back and forth between
the two.

That proxy is called Kerbside and it consists of two components which
each have their own Kolla container. kerbside-api handles business logic
and is a uwsgi app. kerbside-proxy is the SPICE native component. Because
kerbside-proxy is not talking HTTP to clients, and expects TLS encrypted
traffic on the secure port, it uses the frontend certificates to do TLS
itself, and haproxy simply acts as a layer four load balancer.

Change-Id: I73a7a0b521085fd4023b08ab6f8a137d53a8712a
Depends-On: https://review.opendev.org/c/openstack/kolla/+/975495
Closes-Bug: #2131793
Signed-off-by: Michael Still <mikal@stillhq.com>

Deploy Kerbside with Kolla-Ansible.

This change implements the Kerbside Kolla-Ansible deployment role. It is a
fairly large change, but I couldn't find a meaningful way to break it up
into smaller chunks.

The basic idea is that there is a proxy sitting in front of the Nova
hypervisors that can talk the SPICE protocol to clients, lookup where the
console is on the relevant hypervisor, and then build a SPICE connection
to that hypervisor. It then shovels SPICE packets back and forth between
the two.

That proxy is called Kerbside and it consists of two components which
each have their own Kolla container. kerbside-api handles business logic
and is a uwsgi app. kerbside-proxy is the SPICE native component. Because
kerbside-proxy is not talking HTTP to clients, and expects TLS encrypted
traffic on the secure port, it uses the frontend certificates to do TLS
itself, and haproxy simply acts as a layer four load balancer.

This change implements the Kerbside Kolla-Ansible deployment role. It is a
fairly large change, but I couldn't find a meaningful way to break it up
into smaller chunks.

The basic idea is that there is a proxy sitting in front of the Nova
hypervisors that can talk the SPICE protocol to clients, lookup where the
console is on the relevant hypervisor, and then build a SPICE connection
to that hypervisor. It then shovels SPICE packets back and forth between
the two.

That proxy is called Kerbside and it consists of two components which
each have their own Kolla container. kerbside-api handles business logic
and is a uwsgi app. kerbside-proxy is the SPICE native component. Because
kerbside-proxy is not talking HTTP to clients, and expects TLS encrypted
traffic on the secure port, it uses the frontend certificates to do TLS
itself, and haproxy simply acts as a layer four load balancer.

Add Gunicorn using gthreads as wsgi server

If you want to run Swift without eventlet you need to set the
environment variable "USE_EVENTLET=0". For example, using swift-init:

        USE_EVENTLET=0 swift-init restart main

You can also uninstall eventlet before (re-)starting the Swift services
to ensure it is working without it.

Due to a more strict validation of requests, headers and different
encoding a bit of monkey patching is required to match the current
behaviour running Swift with eventlet.

To tune gunicorns a new setting "threads" has been added to the
*-server.conf files. It defaults to 4, but especially the proxy-server
and object-server might be more performant using a higher setting. Note
that this is the number of threads per worker; the number of workers is
by default set to the number of CPU-cores.

Functional tests (still requiring eventlet at this point) should pass
with this implementation, except for the xprofile middleware which
depends on eventlet.

This implementation does not yet work with EC; this needs additional
changes to support 100-Continue requests and will be added in a
followup.

Signed-off-by: Christian Schwede <cschwede@mailbox.org>

Add Gunicorn using gthreads as wsgi server

If you want to run Swift without eventlet you need to set the
environment variable "USE_EVENTLET=0". For example, using swift-init:

        USE_EVENTLET=0 swift-init restart main

You can also uninstall eventlet before (re-)starting the Swift services
to ensure it is working without it.

Due to a more strict validation of requests, headers and different
encoding a bit of monkey patching is required to match the current
behaviour running Swift with eventlet.

To tune gunicorns a new setting "threads" has been added to the
*-server.conf files. It defaults to 4, but especially the proxy-server
and object-server might be more performant using a higher setting. Note
that this is the number of threads per worker; the number of workers is
by default set to the number of CPU-cores.

Functional tests (still requiring eventlet at this point) should pass
with this implementation, except for the xprofile middleware which
depends on eventlet.

This implementation does not yet work with EC; this needs additional
changes to support 100-Continue requests and will be added in a
followup.

to the backends even though we're not terminating tls on the haproxy
load balancer. Hopefully this will give us better x forwarded for
information which can be useful for debugging.

Rebase onto the current Anubis-era gitea vhost (which proxies to Anubis
at http://[::1]:10000/ rather than directly to gitea:3000) and except
IPv6 localhost (::1) in addition to 127.0.0.1 from the PROXY protocol
requirement. The functional tests connect to the backend directly, e.g.
`git clone https://localhost:3081`, where localhost resolves to ::1;
without that exception mod_remoteip's RemoteIPProxyProtocol drops those
header-less connections and system-config-run-gitea fails. The haproxy
load balancer is deliberately not excepted so mod_remoteip can still
recover the real client address for proxied traffic; its health checks
work because send-proxy also prepends the PROXY header to httpchk
connections.

Bind the balance_git_https listener as separate native IPv4 (0.0.0.0:443)
and IPv6 (:::443 v6only) sockets rather than a single dual-stack :::443.
On a dual-stack socket the kernel presents IPv4 peers as IPv4-mapped IPv6
(::ffff:A.B.C.D), so send-proxy emits `PROXY TCP6 ::ffff:...`, which
released Apache mod_remoteip rejects with AH03500 (its TCP6 address
charset has no '.'), aborting the connection -- including the gitea-lb
testinfra requests to 127.0.0.1 and every real IPv4 client once PROXY
protocol is enabled. Native sockets make haproxy emit `PROXY TCP4
A.B.C.D` for v4 clients, which mod_remoteip accepts; IPv6 clients still
get a native TCP6 header.

Set the backend proxy_string to 'send-proxy' only, not 'ssl send-proxy'.
The frontend bind has no 'ssl'/'crt', so in mode tcp haproxy relays the
byte stream and TLS is end-to-end between the client and gitea's Apache.
Adding 'ssl' to the server line makes haproxy open a second TLS session
to the backend and write the client's already-encrypted bytes into it;
Apache then decrypts the outer layer and reads the client's ClientHello
as a plaintext request, answering in cleartext to a client waiting for a
ServerHello. That surfaced as curl exit 35 in testinfra with nothing at
all in gitea's ssl error log. The existing check-ssl is unaffected: it
governs the health check, not the data path.

Change-Id: Ic223a7723babd10f0e7f010925462594c384f0de
Signed-off-by: Anil Belur <abelur@linuxfoundation.org>

Use Haproxy PROXY Protocol with Gitea

Haproxy supports the PROXY protocol which sends useful proxy information
to the backends even though we're not terminating tls on the haproxy
load balancer. Hopefully this will give us better x forwarded for
information which can be useful for debugging.

Rebase onto the current Anubis-era gitea vhost (which proxies to Anubis
at http://[::1]:10000/ rather than directly to gitea:3000) and except
IPv6 localhost (::1) in addition to 127.0.0.1 from the PROXY protocol
requirement. The functional tests connect to the backend directly, e.g.
`git clone https://localhost:3081`, where localhost resolves to ::1;
without that exception mod_remoteip's RemoteIPProxyProtocol drops those
header-less connections and system-config-run-gitea fails. The haproxy
load balancer is deliberately not excepted so mod_remoteip can still
recover the real client address for proxied traffic; its health checks
work because send-proxy also prepends the PROXY header to httpchk
connections.

Bind the balance_git_https listener as separate native IPv4 (0.0.0.0:443)
and IPv6 (:::443 v6only) sockets rather than a single dual-stack :::443.
On a dual-stack socket the kernel presents IPv4 peers as IPv4-mapped IPv6
(::ffff:A.B.C.D), so send-proxy emits `PROXY TCP6 ::ffff:...`, which
released Apache mod_remoteip rejects with AH03500 (its TCP6 address
charset has no '.'), aborting the connection -- including the gitea-lb
testinfra requests to 127.0.0.1 and every real IPv4 client once PROXY
protocol is enabled. Native sockets make haproxy emit `PROXY TCP4
A.B.C.D` for v4 clients, which mod_remoteip accepts; IPv6 clients still
get a native TCP6 header.

Set the backend proxy_string to 'send-proxy' only, not 'ssl send-proxy'.
The frontend bind has no 'ssl'/'crt', so in mode tcp haproxy relays the
byte stream and TLS is end-to-end between the client and gitea's Apache.
Adding 'ssl' to the server line makes haproxy open a second TLS session
to the backend and write the client's already-encrypted bytes into it;
Apache then decrypts the outer layer and reads the client's ClientHello
as a plaintext request, answering in cleartext to a client waiting for a
ServerHello. That surfaced as curl exit 35 in testinfra with nothing at
all in gitea's ssl error log. The existing check-ssl is unaffected: it
governs the health check, not the data path.

Do not emit RemoteIPTrustedProxy for the load balancers. That directive
only gates the header-based path (RemoteIPHeader, e.g. X-Forwarded-For),
and no RemoteIPHeader is set here, so the lines were inert. Access to
port 3081 is already restricted to the gitea-lb group by
iptables_extra_allowed_groups, and RemoteIPProxyProtocolExceptions is
what scopes PROXY header trust. Leaving them in would suggest the client
address depends on them, which it does not.

Preliminary benchmarking indicates noticeable performance gains (~15%)

TODO: if sessions aren't supported at build time, return stub sessions
that use the old API, so pyeclib users can migrate to the new API even
if their liberasurecode hasn't updated yet.

Assisted-by: Claude:claude-4.6-sonnet claude-code-2.1.92
Signed-off-by: Tim Burke <tim.burke@gmail.com>
Change-Id: Ib1e5e47431c00f68d4b1405a5e8f9db369d1500c

Introduce session support

If the built against a liberasurecode library that supports sessions,
those are available. Preliminary benchmarking indicates noticeable
performance gains (~15%) when using liberasurecode sessions.

If not, a compatibility layer is still provided to aid developers in
transitioning to using sessions, with a warning that pyeclib should be
built against newer liberasurecode. The old, non-session API is then
used, but requirements around owning threads and maximum buffer sizes
are enforced.

revisions.message:
Stop looking for remote index with wheels

When we are building wheels, we do not need to check remote index from
containers at all, as all expected packages are expected to be present
on repo containers.

At the moment pip also checks remote index for each package when
searching for versions, which adds overhead and execution time.

Tests on placement role showed, that execution time has reduced around 7
seconds for the venv rebuild solely.

Change-Id: Id399c4440e8b66ae47a07bb14c9246fa610f45dd
Signed-off-by: Dmitriy Rabotyagov <dmitriy.rabotyagov@cleura.com>

Use PEP503 Simple Repository format for wheels

When we are building wheels, we do not need to check remote index from
containers at all, as all expected packages are expected to be present
on repo containers.

With that, current proces of find-links takes quite some extra time
to look for wheel content, producing series of requests toward both
the local repo container, but also remote PyPi index.

In order to limit external communication along with removing overhead,
we are forming wheels according to PEP 503 Simple Index, while keeping
backwards compatability.
Wheels inside of the simple folder are symlinks to old wheels folder.

Removed most tenant_id code from neutron-lib, including:

  tenant_id and project_id keys in API requests
- Any tenant_id attributes in API definitions have been
  changed to project_id
- HasProject class can no longer set or get tenant_id
- get_collection will no longer populate tenant_id
- resource_fields will no longer populate tenant_id
- Returned dictionaries will no longer have tenant_id

Cleaned-up tests accordingly.

- get_collection will no longer populate tenant_id
- resource_fields will no longer populate tenant_id
- Returned dictionaries will no longer have tenant_id

revisions.message:
Add kerbside CI scenario jobs.

Adds three non-voting Zuul jobs that deploy kolla-ansible AIO with
enable_kerbside set to true on Debian Trixie, Ubuntu Noble, and Rocky
10. The jobs follow the masakari scenario layout: a base job that
sets scenario: kerbside, three distro-specific jobs using the
existing single-node 16GB AIO nodesets, and a project-template
collecting them under check (not gate) while the jobs are still
being shaken down.

The jobs trigger via files: !inherit on changes to kerbside and
nova roles and group_vars, plus the kerbside-specific cert
files. globals-default.j2 gets a {% if scenario == "kerbside" %}
block that enables kerbside and sets nova_console to spice.
tests/run.yml is extended so openstack_core_tested includes the
kerbside scenario, which causes init-core-openstack.sh and the
kolla-ansible-tempest role to run with the default .*smoke.* regex
inherited from the base job.

The base job sets kolla_build_images: true with a 10800 second
timeout to match the existing non-voting image-building jobs (the
SPICE-enabled kolla images are not yet in the published image set,
so kerbside CI builds them locally). Combined with a Depends-On
line in the Gerrit submission pointing at the matching kolla
change, this gives Zuul speculative execution end-to-end: the
depended-on kolla patch is applied to the kolla source tree on
the test node, images are built from it and pushed to the local
primary:4000 registry, and the need_build_image branch of
globals-default.j2 flips docker_namespace and docker_registry to
use that registry.

Future work: add kerbside-specific Tempest tests via a plugin and
extend kolla_ansible_tempest_regex once the smoke baseline is
trusted.

Prompt: Michael asked me to draft the new tempest test in
src/kolla-ansible/ and then commit it here so he can produce a
patch from the resulting diff. A follow-up asked to enable
image-building plus the timeout bump used by the existing
non-voting image-building kolla-ansible jobs, so the kerbside
scenario can exercise an in-flight kolla change via Depends-On.

Assisted-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context, medium effort) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context, medium effort) <noreply@anthropic.com>

revisions.message:
Run the spice-direct tempest test in the kerbside scenario.

The kerbside scenario jobs added in I1784562d already deploy
kolla-ansible with enable_kerbside=yes and nova_console=spice, then
run the default ".*smoke.*" Tempest regex. This adds the SPICE
coverage that motivated the scenario in the first place.

The test itself lives in upstream Tempest as
tempest.api.compute.admin.test_spice.SpiceDirectConsoleTestJSON
and exercises the full spice-direct console flow: create an
instance, request a console token, exchange it for hypervisor
connection details, and complete a SPICE protocol handshake
against the returned hypervisor host:port. It skips itself unless
CONF.compute_feature_enabled.spice_console is True, and nothing
in kolla-ansible currently sets that — python-tempestconf does
not auto-detect SPICE from the cloud.

Two changes are needed:

1. roles/kolla-ansible-tempest gains a new
   kolla_ansible_tempest_discover_overrides list, whose entries
   are appended as positional "section.option value" arguments to
   discover-tempest-config. This is the same override syntax the
   role already uses for compute.build_timeout, so no new code
   path is introduced — just a per-scenario knob.

2. zuul.d/scenarios/kerbside.yaml sets that override to enable
   compute-feature-enabled.spice_console and extends
   kolla_ansible_tempest_regex so the spice test is selected
   alongside the existing smoke tests. The test has no smoke
   decorator, so without this it would be discovered but not
   run.

Note that this test _does_not_ validate that Kerbside is deployed
and working correctly. That's the next step after this one.

Prompt: Michael asked for a follow-up patch to patch156 that
actually runs the spice-direct Tempest test (originally added to
Tempest for Nova's CI) inside the kerbside scenario.

revisions.message:
Run a Kerbside-fronted SPICE tempest test in the kerbside scenario.

Patch157 enabled the upstream spice-direct test, which speaks SPICE
to the hypervisor port Nova returns. That validates Nova's
spice-direct plumbing but does not exercise Kerbside at all. This
adds a follow-up test that proves the URL Nova returns is fronted
by Kerbside's haproxy and that Kerbside is answering as SPICE.

The test lives in the kerbside-tempest-plugin, a separate releasable
in the shakenfist/kerbside repository whose version is tied to
Kerbside's via setuptools_scm. The plugin contributes one test,
kerbside_tempest_plugin.tests.api.test_spice_via_kerbside, which:

1. Calls Nova's get-remote-console with spice-direct/spice.
2. HTTPS-GETs the returned URL using the Kolla-Ansible CA
   (/etc/kolla/certificates/ca/root.crt by default), which is the
   trust chain for the haproxy front-end Kerbside terminates.
3. Parses the .vv file Kerbside serves at that URL, extracts the
   SPICE host, tls-port, and embedded CA certificate.
4. Opens a TLS connection to that host:tls-port trusting only the
   embedded CA, sends a SpiceLinkMess for the main channel, and
   reads back the SpiceLinkReply header. A SPICE magic in the reply
   proves Kerbside is talking SPICE.

The test does not yet authenticate or route through to a hypervisor
console -- that needs the auth ticket from the .vv file and a fuller
walk of the SPICE protocol, which will land separately backed by
shakenfist/ryll and shakenfist/uncalibrated-sextant.

Three changes are needed in kolla-ansible:

1. roles/kolla-ansible-tempest gains a new kolla_ansible_tempest_plugins
   list. Entries are appended to the pip install of the tempest venv,
   so callers can install tempest plugins from PyPI, git URLs, or
   local paths.

2. zuul.d/scenarios/kerbside.yaml uses that list to install
   kerbside-tempest-plugin from the shakenfist/kerbside repo,
   pulling from the develop branch.

3. The same scenario file extends kolla_ansible_tempest_regex so the
   new test is selected alongside the existing smoke set and the
   spice-direct test added in patch157.

Prompt: Michael asked for a follow-up to patch157 that runs a
tempest test through the Kerbside haproxy front-end, after we
discussed whether to ship it as an in-tree patch against tempest or
as a separate tempest plugin. We landed on a plugin in the kerbside
repo, packaged as its own releasable but sharing kerbside's version
via a setuptools_scm root pointing at the parent directory.

Run a Kerbside-fronted SPICE tempest test in the kerbside scenario.

Patch157 enabled the upstream spice-direct test, which speaks SPICE
to the hypervisor port Nova returns. That validates Nova's
spice-direct plumbing but does not exercise Kerbside at all. This
adds a follow-up test that proves the URL Nova returns is fronted
by Kerbside's haproxy and that Kerbside is answering as SPICE.

The test lives in the kerbside-tempest-plugin, a separate releasable
in the shakenfist/kerbside repository whose version is tied to
Kerbside's via setuptools_scm. The plugin contributes one test,
kerbside_tempest_plugin.tests.api.test_spice_via_kerbside, which:

1. Calls Nova's get-remote-console with spice-direct/spice.
2. HTTPS-GETs the returned URL using the Kolla-Ansible CA
   (/etc/kolla/certificates/ca/root.crt by default), which is the
   trust chain for the haproxy front-end Kerbside terminates.
3. Parses the .vv file Kerbside serves at that URL, extracts the
   SPICE host, tls-port, and embedded CA certificate.
4. Opens a TLS connection to that host:tls-port trusting only the
   embedded CA, sends a SpiceLinkMess for the main channel, and
   reads back the SpiceLinkReply header. A SPICE magic in the reply
   proves Kerbside is talking SPICE.

The test does not yet authenticate or route through to a hypervisor
console -- that needs the auth ticket from the .vv file and a fuller
walk of the SPICE protocol, which will land separately backed by
shakenfist/ryll and shakenfist/uncalibrated-sextant.

Three changes are needed in kolla-ansible:

1. roles/kolla-ansible-tempest gains a new kolla_ansible_tempest_plugins
   list. Entries are appended to the pip install of the tempest venv,
   so callers can install tempest plugins from PyPI, git URLs, or
   local paths.

2. zuul.d/scenarios/kerbside.yaml uses that list to install
   kerbside-tempest-plugin from the shakenfist/kerbside repo,
   pulling from the develop branch.

3. The same scenario file extends kolla_ansible_tempest_regex so the
   new test is selected alongside the existing smoke set and the
   spice-direct test added in patch157.

Prompt: Michael asked for a follow-up to patch157 that runs a
tempest test through the Kerbside haproxy front-end, after we
discussed whether to ship it as an in-tree patch against tempest or
as a separate tempest plugin. We landed on a plugin in the kerbside
repo, packaged as its own releasable but sharing kerbside's version
via a setuptools_scm root pointing at the parent directory.

to the hypervisor port Nova returns. That validates Nova's
spice-direct plumbing but does not exercise Kerbside at all. This
adds a follow-up test that proves the URL Nova returns is fronted
by Kerbside's haproxy and that Kerbside is answering as SPICE.

The test lives in the kerbside-tempest-plugin, a separate releasable
in the shakenfist/kerbside repository whose version is tied to
Kerbside's via setuptools_scm. The plugin contributes one test,
kerbside_tempest_plugin.tests.api.test_spice_via_kerbside, which:

1. Calls Nova's get-remote-console with spice-direct/spice.
2. HTTPS-GETs the returned URL using the Kolla-Ansible CA
   (/etc/kolla/certificates/ca/root.crt by default), which is the
   trust chain for the haproxy front-end Kerbside terminates.
3. Parses the .vv file Kerbside serves at that URL, extracts the
   SPICE host, tls-port, and embedded CA certificate.
4. Opens a TLS connection to that host:tls-port trusting only the
   embedded CA, sends a SpiceLinkMess for the main channel, and
   reads back the SpiceLinkReply header. A SPICE magic in the reply
   proves Kerbside is talking SPICE.

The test does not yet authenticate or route through to a hypervisor
console -- that needs the auth ticket from the .vv file and a fuller
walk of the SPICE protocol, which will land separately backed by
shakenfist/ryll and shakenfist/uncalibrated-sextant.

Three changes are needed in kolla-ansible:

1. roles/kolla-ansible-tempest gains a new kolla_ansible_tempest_plugins
   list. Entries are appended to the pip install of the tempest venv,
   so callers can install tempest plugins from PyPI, git URLs, or
   local paths.

2. zuul.d/scenarios/kerbside.yaml uses that list to install
   kerbside-tempest-plugin from the shakenfist/kerbside repo,
   pulling from the develop branch.

3. The same scenario file extends kolla_ansible_tempest_regex so the
   new test is selected alongside the existing smoke set and the
   spice-direct test added in patch157.

Prompt: Now add a tempest test which runs a SPICE console connection
through the Kerbside haproxy front-end, after we discussed whether
to ship it as an in-tree patch against tempest or as a separate
tempest plugin. We landed on a plugin in the kerbside repo, packaged
as its own releasable but sharing kerbside's version via a
setuptools_scm root pointing at the parent directory.

revisions.message:
Support cold migration with virtiofs shares

Cold migration was blocked for instances with virtiofs
share attachments because Nova never granted Manila
access or mounted shares on the destination host.

This change lifts that restriction with a lazy cleanup
strategy: shares stay mounted on the source until confirm.
On the destination, _finish_resize() grants Manila access
and mounts shares before calling the driver. Revert cleans
up the destination; the source retains its mounts
throughout.

New helpers _grant_share_access() and _revoke_share_access()
encapsulate Manila access operations without side effects
(no status transitions, notifications, or DB changes).
The existing allow_share()/deny_share() are refactored to
call these helpers.

The @block_shares_not_supported() decorator on resize() is
replaced with an inline SERVICE_VERSION 73 check, gating
cold migration on all computes supporting it.

The share_info parameter is added to finish_migration() and
finish_revert_migration() in the base driver, libvirt,
VMware, and fake drivers so the destination can include
virtiofs filesystems in the domain XML.

Partially-implements: blueprint virtiofs-cold-migration
Signed-off-by: Goutham Pacha Ravi <gouthampravi@gmail.com>
Assisted-by: Claude Opus 4.6
Change-Id: I2cda35fa0c2e080a67418d557cb9030b11f31394

Support cold migration with virtiofs shares

Lift the restriction on cold migration and resize for
instances with virtiofs share attachments. On the
destination, _finish_resize() grants Manila access and
mounts shares. Revert cleans up the destination; the
source retains its mounts until confirm. Same-host resize
skips redundant grant/mount/unmount/revoke operations.

A two-layer gate controls access: API microversion 2.104
signals client support, and SERVICE_VERSION 73 ensures
all computes can handle cold migration with shares.

Partially-implements: blueprint virtiofs-cold-migration

Add cold migration and resize tests for virtiofs shares

Add four scenario tests for cold migration and resize
with virtiofs share attachments:
- cold migrate + confirm
- cold migrate + revert
- resize (cross-host, different flavor) + confirm
- resize + revert

These tests are gated on [compute-feature-enabled]
cold_migration and require a multinode deployment.

A new multinode CI job (manila-tempest-plugin-multinode-
virtiofs-lvm) is added to exercise these tests with the
LVM share driver on two compute nodes with
file_backed_memory enabled for virtiofs support.

revisions.message:
Add Weka share driver

Adds a Manila share driver for Weka storage, supporting two protocols:

- WEKAFS: the WekaFS POSIX kernel client (sub-250 µs latency, full POSIX
  semantics, native quota enforcement). Requires the WekaFS kernel module
  on the Manila host.
- NFS: standard NFS v3 exports via Weka's built-in NFS gateway. Works on
  all kernel versions with no additional client software.

The driver operates in DHSS=false mode. Weka filesystems are mapped
directly to Manila shares. Supported operations include create/delete,
extend/shrink, ensure, snapshots, revert-to-snapshot, create-from-snapshot,
manage/unmanage, and capacity reporting.

Also adds WEKAFS to SUPPORTED_SHARE_PROTOCOLS in constants.py, RST
admin documentation, and updates the share backends feature support
mapping.

Implements: blueprint weka-share-driver
Change-Id: Ic3f85449009b3a15a1219a01b8b4217132b41899
Signed-off-by: Itai Weisman <itai.weisman@weka.io>

Add Weka share driver

Adds a Manila share driver for Weka storage, supporting two protocols:

- WEKAFS: the WekaFS POSIX kernel client (sub-250 µs latency, full POSIX
  semantics, native quota enforcement). Requires the WekaFS kernel module
  on the Manila host.
- NFS: standard NFS v3 exports via Weka's built-in NFS gateway. Works on
  all kernel versions with no additional client software.

The driver operates in DHSS=false mode. Weka filesystems are mapped
directly to Manila shares. Supported operations include create/delete,
extend/shrink, ensure, snapshots, revert-to-snapshot,
create-from-snapshot, manage/unmanage, and capacity reporting.

WEKAFS shares are isolated per tenant. Each Manila project is mapped to
its own Weka organization, and WEKAFS filesystems are created with
authentication required inside that organization, so a mount token
scoped to one project cannot mount another project's shares -- access is
enforced at the Weka organization boundary. The per-project mount
credential is returned to the tenant as the access_key of a WEKAFS
access rule (self-service, no operator hand-off). This requires a
multi-tenant Weka cluster and the weka_org_admin_secret option, from
which the per-organization credentials are derived; the driver refuses
to start if it is unset. NFS shares use IP-based access rules.

Also adds WEKAFS to SUPPORTED_SHARE_PROTOCOLS in constants.py, RST admin
documentation, and updates the share backends feature support mapping.

- WEKAFS: the WekaFS POSIX kernel client (sub-250 µs latency, full POSIX
  semantics, native quota enforcement). Requires the WekaFS kernel module
  on the Manila host.

access_key (that field is reserved upstream for cephx keys).

security policy that admits only the client source IPs it names, denying
all others at native mount time. --access-level is honored (ro installs
a read-only policy); ip rules are IPv4-only. Alternatively, a share type
may reference a shared, reusable group policy via the
weka:security_policy_group extra spec, defined by the
weka_security_policy_group option.

documentation, and updates the share backends feature support mapping.

update_access honors both modes of the driver contract. In incremental
mode the driver applies add_rules, delete_rules and update_rules. When
add_rules and delete_rules are both empty -- as they are when the access
level changes for every rule on a share -- the driver instead reconciles
the backend down to access_rules, removing the export permissions,
client groups and security-policy addresses that no longer correspond to
a rule, so a revoked rule cannot leave working access behind on the
cluster. Shares whose type sets weka:security_policy_group are exempt:
those policies are shared between shares, so reconciling one share's
rules against them would revoke the others.

documentation, and updates the share backends feature support mapping.

revisions.message:
Maintenance: add node_maintenance table

Introduce a node_maintenance table that records maintenance entries
on a node as discrete rows. The boolean node.maintenance and
node.maintenance_reason columns stay at the user-facing API surface;
mirroring into the new table happens in a follow-up change.

The table carries a type column to distinguish categories of
maintenance and an initial 'legacy' constant labels entries that
mirror the existing boolean. Future types are introduced by
follow-up changes alongside the behaviour they require.

A migration backfills one 'legacy' entry per node currently in
maintenance, preserving its maintenance_reason verbatim.

revisions.message:
FlashArray: add Changed Block Tracking backup support

Implement the CBT incremental backup driver methods (get_cbt_extents,
create_cbt_snapshot, delete_cbt_snapshot) for the Everpure FlashArray
driver using the array's volumes/diff API. Opaque reference identifiers
from the backup framework are mapped deterministically to length-safe
array snapshot names, and adjacent changed extents are consolidated to
bound the RPC payload.

Add a pure_cbt_diff_block_size option to control diff granularity. On

revisions.message:
Increase PBKDF2-SHA512 default iterations to 600,000

Keystone's PBKDF2-SHA512 password hasher previously used 25,000
iterations as its default, well below the OWASP 2023 recommendation
of 600,000 for PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512.  While PBKDF2 with HMAC is
considered quantum-safe, Grover's algorithm provides a quadratic
speedup for brute-force search, making a high iteration count
important for long-term security.

This change:

* Raises the default round count from 25,000 to 600,000 via the
  new public constant ``pbkdf2.DEFAULT_ROUNDS``.  The value remains
  operator-configurable through ``[identity] password_hash_rounds``.

* Adds ``Sha512.needs_rehash()`` to detect hashes computed with
  fewer iterations than the current target, and a module-level
  ``password_hashing.needs_rehash()`` that additionally detects
  algorithm mismatches.

* Transparently rehashes outdated passwords on the next successful
  authentication by updating the ``password_hash`` column of the
  current Password record in place, leaving password-history,
  expiry, and created_at metadata untouched.

The ~24x increase in hashing work per authentication is expected
and intentional.  Operators should benchmark their hardware and
tune ``[identity] password_hash_rounds`` if the new default causes
unacceptable latency.

OSPRH-27983

Change-Id: I43bf8f575eeb7a026c28140007dc0f0fccdf5144
Signed-off-by: Mauricio Harley <mharley@redhat.com>

Change-Id: I43bf8f575eeb7a026c28140007dc0f0fccdf5144
Signed-off-by: Mauricio Harley <mharley@redhat.com>

Increase PBKDF2-SHA512 default iterations to 600,000

Raise the default iteration count for PBKDF2-SHA512 password hashing
from 25,000 to 600,000, matching the OWASP 2023 recommendation.  The
higher count strengthens resistance to brute-force attacks, including
quantum-accelerated search via Grover's algorithm.

Existing passwords are transparently rehashed on next successful
authentication thanks to the rehash infrastructure introduced in
the companion patch.  Operators may tune the value via
[identity] password_hash_rounds.

Expected authentication latency impact: 0.3-0.8 s per login on
modern hardware.

HPE: Snapshot features for Alletra MP driver & Added support for new snapshot_inherit_share_access share type

Includes a new share type snapshot_inherit_share_access. Setting this will block mountable snapshot access rule modification for the share.

Following features are included to the Alletra Driver
1. Create/Delete snapshot.
2. Manage/Unmanage snapshot..
3. Revert to snapshot.
4. Mountable snapshot.

s3api: User Checksum Persistence on MPUs

Swift does checksum validation on UploadPart during an
Multi-Part Object Upload, but it does not presist that checksum
metadata after.

See AWS Docs:
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/checking-object-integrity-upload.html

s3api: User Checksum Persistence on MPUs

Swift does checksum validation on UploadPart during an
Multi-Part Object Upload, but it does not presist that checksum
metadata after.

Like checksum persistence on full object uploads,
This patch allows users of the s3api to specify a checksum
algorithm during a Multi Part Upload of both
FULL_OBJECT checksum types and also COMPOSITE checksum types.
A user can also just test checksums on UploadPart requests
instead of the entire MPU lifecycle.

We persist s3api sysmeta headers on the MPU manifest
and use that to decide what checksum algorithm to
enforce in later stages of the MPU lifecycle, and how
to validate the final checksum. We also use checksum
metadata from override headers in 'content-type' to
get metadata during listing of MPU parts.

This patch does not add support for checksum computation
for UploadPartCopy when the Copy Source does not have or
match the checksum algorithm on the MPU.

See AWS Docs:
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/checking-object-integrity-upload.html

s3api: User Checksum Persistence on MPUs

Swift does checksum validation on UploadPart during an
Multi-Part Object Upload, but it does not presist that checksum
metadata after.

Like checksum persistence on full object uploads,
This patch allows users of the s3api to specify a checksum
algorithm during a Multi Part Upload of both
FULL_OBJECT checksum types and also COMPOSITE checksum types.
A user can also just insert specific checksums on UploadPart requests
instead the same checksum on each part the entire MPU lifecycle.

We persist s3api sysmeta headers on the MPU manifest
and use that to decide what checksum algorithm to
enforce in later stages of the MPU lifecycle, and how
to validate the final checksum for the MPU.

This patch does not add support for checksum computation
for UploadPartCopy when the Copy Source does not have or
match the checksum algorithm on the MPU.

The S3 API behavior changes for multipart uploads:

* CreateMultipartUpload accepts x-amz-checksum-algorithm and
  x-amz-checksum-type, persists the selected checksum configuration,
  and returns both values in the response.
* UploadPart validates and persists x-amz-checksum-* values and returns
  the validated checksum in the response. Checksum-aware uploads
  require each part to use the algorithm selected at initiation.
* UploadPartCopy preserves and returns the source checksum when copying
  the complete source object with a compatible checksum algorithm.
* CompleteMultipartUpload persists and returns the completed checksum
  and checksum type. GetObject and HeadObject return these values when
  x-amz-checksum-mode: ENABLED is requested.
* COMPOSITE checksums support CRC32, CRC32C, SHA1, and SHA256.
  FULL_OBJECT checksums support CRC32, CRC32C, and CRC64NVME.
* UploadPartCopy requests and incompatible source checksums return 501.

See AWS Docs:
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/checking-object-integrity-upload.html

s3api: Checksum Persistence on MPUs

Swift does checksum validation on UploadPart during a
Multi-Part Object Upload, but it does not persist that checksum
metadata after.

Like checksum persistence on full object uploads,
This patch allows users of the s3api to specify a checksum
algorithm during a Multi Part Upload of both
FULL_OBJECT checksum types and also COMPOSITE checksum types.
A user can also just insert specific checksums on UploadPart requests
instead the same checksum on each part the entire MPU lifecycle.

We persist s3api sysmeta headers on the MPU manifest
and use that to decide what checksum algorithm to
enforce in later stages of the MPU lifecycle, and how
to validate the final checksum for the MPU.

During CompleteMultipartUpload, SLO gathers each segment’s
checksum metadata and passes the aligned HEAD response headers
to s3api’s manifest hook. s3api validates the stored part checksums
against any client-provided values, calculates and validates
the completed MPU checksum, and persists the resulting checksum
metadata on the final SLO manifest using the footer callback.

This patch does not add support for checksum computation
for UploadPartCopy.

In the event of mismatched proxy servers versions, we attach a
sysmeta sentinel checksum header, also know as 'checksum-upload-id'
to each MPU part that passes through a new proxy server.
On final checksum computation, any part that does not have the
header, will cause the MPU to be completed without the final
checksum.

The S3 API behavior changes for multipart uploads:

* CreateMultipartUpload accepts x-amz-checksum-algorithm and
  x-amz-checksum-type, persists the selected checksum configuration,
  and returns both values in the response.

* UploadPart validates and persists x-amz-checksum-* values and returns
  the validated checksum in the response. Checksum-aware uploads
  of type COMPOSITE require each part to use the algorithm
  selected at initiation. FULL_OBJECT does not require it.

* CompleteMultipartUpload persists and returns the completed checksum
  and checksum type. GetObject and HeadObject return these values when
  x-amz-checksum-mode: ENABLED is requested.

* COMPOSITE checksums support CRC32, CRC32C, SHA1, and SHA256.

* FULL_OBJECT checksums support CRC32, CRC32C, and CRC64NVME.

* FULL_OBJECT checksum usage for MPUs depends on `anycrc` being
  installed in the Swift cluster, if not, a 501 will be thrown on usage attempts.

See AWS Docs:
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/checking-object-integrity-upload.html

revisions.message:
Apply import URI filtering to legacy import tasks

Legacy type=import tasks only ran validate_location_uri, so
import_from could skip the same host/port/path checks used for
modern image import. Route import_from through a small helper that
reuses validate_location_uri then validate_import_uri, and
reject bad URIs early when creating import tasks.

Closes-Bug: #2152110
Assisted-By: Cursor (claude-4.5-sonnet) for tests
Change-Id: I6fbb8a91a49e3df6fa9bb185f7fcd8b1816ad74e
Signed-off-by: Abhishek Kekane <akekane@redhat.com>

revisions.message:
Add upstream EVPN multinode Zuul job

Create a neutron-ovn-evpn-tempest-multinode job to deploy EVPN
on a spine-leaf topology and run tempest scenario tests against it.

The job reuses the same 5-node nodeset and shared playbooks as the
existing BGP job. An abstract base job
(neutron-ovn-bgp-tempest-multinode-base) is extracted to hold the
common infrastructure, with both the BGP and EVPN jobs as children
that only add their feature-specific configuration.

EVPN-specific setup:
- FRR_USE_EVPN enables simple FRR config and VRF kernel module
- OVN agent extension ovn-evpn with ovn_evpn config section
- Loopback IPs and OVS external_ids (ovn-evpn-local-ip,
  ovn-evpn-vxlan-ports) provisioned via the shared pre-run playbook
- L2VPN EVPN address-family added to leaf/spine FRR templates
  behind an enable_evpn conditional
- evpn added to neutron service_plugins

Closes-Bug: OSPRH-31517

Change-Id: Ic9cee636c9b58875c64c7b45280ce5e87f8163d1
Signed-off-by: Eduardo Olivares <eolivare@redhat.com>
Assisted-By: Claude Opus 4.6

Add upstream EVPN multinode Zuul job

Create a neutron-ovn-evpn-tempest-multinode periodic job to deploy
EVPN on a spine-leaf topology and run tempest scenario tests.

The job reuses the same 5-node nodeset and shared playbooks as the
existing BGP job. An abstract base job
(neutron-ovn-bgp-tempest-multinode-base) is extracted to hold the
common infrastructure, with both the BGP and EVPN jobs as children
that only add their feature-specific configuration.

EVPN-specific setup:
- FRR_USE_EVPN enables simple FRR config and VRF kernel module
- OVN agent extension ovn-evpn with ovn_evpn config section
- Loopback IPs and OVS external_ids (ovn-evpn-local-ip,
  ovn-evpn-vxlan-ports) provisioned via the shared pre-run playbook
- L2VPN EVPN address-family on leaf/spine FRR templates
  (activate, route-reflector, advertise-all-vni) for EVPN route
  exchange; no static per-VNI VRF/import/RT in frr.conf
- Spine host prerequisites only: VRF module, VXLAN iptables
  allow, and l3mdev_accept sysctls for cross-VRF TCP/UDP
- EVPN VXLAN uses port 4789 (IANA standard) to match OVN's
  DEFAULT_VXLAN_PORT for remote VTEP discovery; infrastructure
  tunnels use evpn_vxlan_port + 1 to avoid conflicts
- evpn added to neutron service_plugins
- Bump OVN to v26.03.2 and OVS to v3.7.1 for critical EVPN
  data plane fixes (VTEP ports treated as non-local, conntrack
  skip for EVPN traffic, L3 EVPN with non-L2-adjacent VTEPs)

Per-VNI dataplane (VXLAN/bridge/VRF) and FRR VRF BGP config are
intentionally left to dynamic provisioning in tempest
(EVPNVNIProvisioner)

revisions.message:
RBD: server-side copy when uploading a volume to an image

When Glance is backed by the same Ceph cluster as Cinder, uploading a
volume to an image streams the entire volume from Ceph through the
cinder-volume host to the Glance API and back into Ceph. For raw images
this is a pure network round-trip of data that already lives in the
cluster and is prohibitively slow for large volumes.

Add an optional server-side path to RBDDriver.copy_volume_to_image: when
the new ``rbd_glance_pool`` option is set and the image is raw and
uncompressed, snapshot the volume, clone it into the Glance pool,
flatten the clone so it no longer depends on the volume, create the
protected ``snap`` snapshot Glance expects, and register the resulting
RBD location with Glance via the image location API. No image data
crosses the network; the copy is performed entirely within Ceph.

The path is opt-in and only used for raw, uncompressed images sharing
the same Ceph cluster. On any failure the partially created clone and
snapshots are cleaned up and the existing streaming upload is used as a
fallback, so behaviour is unchanged when the option is unset or the
fast path cannot be taken.

Registering the location uses the privileged Glance client, so the
service must be authorized for Glance's add_image_location API
(``[glance]`` credentials with the required role).

Signed-off-by: Maximilian Brandt <maximilian.brandt@cloudandheat.com>

devstack: Configure pci-sim Cyborg PCI testing

Generate generic PCI whitelist entries for pci-sim VFs. Include vendor
and product IDs. Set managed=false by default because the pci-sim VFIO
variant driver requires unmanaged libvirt hostdev mode. This prevents
libvirt from detaching and rebinding the device.

Configure Cyborg Tempest plugin options for the pci-sim Cyborg device
profile and expected PCI IDs when pci-sim Cyborg mode is enabled. Set
Tempest concurrency to 4. This matches the default pci-sim allocation of
four Cyborg VFs and the scenario tests' one-device-per-test usage.

revisions.message:
libvirt: Support Cyborg PCI ARQ managed mode

Request Cyborg API microversion 2.4 for ARQ GET requests when the Cyborg
server supports it. Version 2.4 includes the optional managed key in PCI
ARQ attach handle information.

Use that managed key when generating libvirt PCI hostdev XML for Cyborg
ARQs. When managed is false, Nova creates hostdev XML with managed=no so
libvirt does not detach and rebind devices that must remain bound to a
host VFIO variant driver. Missing managed data continues to default to
managed mode for compatibility with older Cyborg services.

Add libvirt functional coverage for managed=false, managed=true, omitted
managed data, and a create/delete lifecycle with managed=false.

Implements: blueprint support-vfio-variant-driver-managed-mode-via-cyborg

Add DPLL pin priority configuration parameters

Add section=dpll parameters on clock PTP instances to control
zl3073x DPLL pin priorities and states. Parameters are grouped
by function: gnss, synce, ptp (SDP), and ext (external).

Client-side validation enforces priority range 0-14 and state
values (selectable, disconnected). The puppet networking module
generates a JSON config consumed by the enforcement script.

Test Plan:
PASS: Unit tests (8 tests in TestDpllPinConfig, tox py39)
PASS: Add all 4 priority params, apply, verify pins changed on
      GNR-D hardware (dx-028, E825/zl3073x)
PASS: Reject invalid param name, out-of-range priority, bad state
PASS: Partial config (only gnss set) does not touch other pins
PASS: Graceful behavior on non-GNR-D (VDM, no zl3073x pins)

DNM == Migrate QoS with placement tests from tempest

NOTE: this patch is similar to I02d034482fe15c87f766d814ab9b89bc13382e73
but removing the dependency to the Neutron patch.

As agreed on neutron meeting [1] better to have tests on
neutron-tempest-plugin for better neutron control to review/merge,
track in CI, and adjust according to neutron needs.
Tests migrated from [2].

Set configurations to execute tests in CI for both openvswitch/ovn jobs.

From migrated configurations:
1) replaced duplicate
`provider_net_base_segmentation_id` with local plugin's
`provider_net_base_segm_id` already set in CI.
2) And set `qos_placement_physnet` default to fit CI `public` value.

Notice 2 dependency patches devstack/neutron fixes needed for tests to pass.

[1] https://meetings.opendev.org/meetings/networking/2026/networking.2026-02-10-14.00.log.html#l-182
[2] https://opendev.org/openstack/tempest/src/commit/95208710c0/tempest/scenario/test_network_qos_placement.py#L90

revisions.message:
Switch manager pod from bash init.sh to baomon run

Replace the legacy bash init.sh script with baomon run as the manager
pod's main process. This eliminates the bash-based unseal/rekey logic
and uses the Go-based lifecycle manager instead.

storage.

new generation-based key shard architecture. The baomon ConfigMap
gains SecretPrefix and GenerationPrefix fields for the generation
secret naming scheme.

Signed-off-by: Dmitriy Rabotyagov <dmitriy.rabotyagov@cleura.com>

Respect Depends-On for service projects

Historically OpenStack-Ansible was not respecting Depends-On for service
projects. This was related to quite some level of complexity
related with our SHA pinning process, where we do not want to
consume HEAD/master version, but pinned SHA during development to keep
CI stable.

However, there're quite some cases where we want to ensure, that patches
to services solve issue for us, thus respecting Depends-On is quite
important to have.

In order to solve the usecase, a helper module has being written
for bootstrap-host role, which parses previosly recorded
osa-job-vars.yml from filesystem, which is a snapshot of zuul vars,
and records <service>_git_install_branch
for it to be further written down to user_variables.

Add ASGI application entry point for Placement API

Adds placement.asgi.api:application, an ASGI entry point that wraps the
existing WSGI application using oslo_service.asgi.wrap_wsgi(). This
enables serving the Placement API under modern ASGI servers such as
Hypercorn while preserving all middleware, authentication, and API
behavior unchanged.

Usage:
  $ hypercorn placement.asgi.api:application --bind 0.0.0.0:8778

The existing WSGI entry point (placement.wsgi.api:application) remains
available and unchanged for deployers using uwsgi, gunicorn, or mod_wsgi.

ASGI mode requires eventlet to be disabled. Placement already runs
without eventlet by default, so no additional configuration is needed.

Also adds a voting tempest-integrated-placement-asgi gate job that runs
the full integrated placement tempest suite with the API served under
Hypercorn instead of uWSGI.

Depends-On: https://review.opendev.org/c/openstack/oslo.service/+/995128
Depends-On: https://review.opendev.org/c/openstack/devstack/+/995132

Adds placement.asgi.api:application, an ASGI entry point that wraps the
existing WSGI application using oslo_service.asgi.wrap_wsgi(). This
enables serving the Placement API under modern ASGI servers such as
Hypercorn while preserving all middleware, authentication, and API
behavior unchanged.

available and unchanged for deployers using uwsgi, gunicorn, or mod_wsgi.

without eventlet by default, so no additional configuration is needed.

The ASGI entry point clears sys.argv before initializing the service
as a defensive measure against ASGI servers passing their own CLI
arguments (--bind, --workers, etc.) which could confuse oslo.config.

Also adds a voting tempest-integrated-placement-asgi gate job that runs
the full integrated placement tempest suite with the API served under
Hypercorn instead of uWSGI.

Netapp: Implement ZAPI to REST gaps

Implement REST equivalents for the following ZAPI-only methods:
- is_svm_dr_supported
- is_svm_migrate_supported
- get_data_lif_details_for_nodes
- get_volume_autosize_attributes
- list_vservers
- configure_cifs_options
- default_ad_site
- is_kerberos_enabled
- modify_volume (volume autosize reset now uses public REST endpoint
  /storage/volumes/{uuid} on supported ONTAP versions, falling back

revisions.message:
Add deferred puppet trigger for Keystone federation on upgrade

Change-Id: Ib7ead1d57b3a2926808beefb2c27afc3500bccab
Signed-off-by: Felipe Vasconcelos <Felipe.Vasconcelos@windriver.com>

Add deferred puppet trigger for Keystone federation on upgrade

After oidc-auth-apps is applied, the lifecycle plugin triggers openstack::keystone::server::runtime to create federation resources (IdP, mapping, protocol) in Keystone.

On fresh install, the operation/post hook provides direct conductor access for immediate puppet trigger. During upgrades (app update), operation/post does not fire — only manifest/post fires with conductor_obj=None. In this case, a flag file is created at /opt/platform/config/<ver>/.federation_config_required that the conductor periodic audit picks up within ~60 seconds of activate completing.

Both hooks call post_apply_operation (writes OIDC login config) and post_apply (puppet trigger or flag creation) for resilience against framework ordering changes.

The RPC fallback (update_service_config via RabbitMQ) is removed as RabbitMQ is unavailable during deploy-activate, causing the sysinv process to hang in an infinite AMQP retry loop.

Test plan:
PASS: Fresh install Bullseye AIO-SX, apply oidc-auth-apps, verify federation resources created immediately via operation/post.
PASS: Upgrade 26.03 to 26.09, verify federation resources created automatically via flag-file mechanism (~60s after activate-done).
PASS: Verify OIDC login config written on both install and upgrade. PASS: Verify flag file removed after conductor processes it.
PASS: Re-apply oidc-auth-apps, verify idempotent (no duplicates).
PASS: Normal credential-based login unaffected.

bump in requirements.txt.

revisions.message:
letsencrypt: Add ACME dns-01 challenge support

So far the letsencrypt role only supported the ACME http-01 challenge,
which requires Horizon, the letsencrypt-webserver container and HAProxy
proxying of /.well-known/acme-challenge.

This adds support for the ACME dns-01 challenge, selected with the new
letsencrypt_challenge variable (default http-01, so existing deployments
are unaffected). The implementation is provider agnostic: any DNS
provider supported by the bundled lego binary can be used by naming it in
letsencrypt_dns_provider and supplying the environment variables it
expects through the generic letsencrypt_lego_dns_environment
mapping.

When the dns-01 challenge is selected, the letsencrypt-webserver
container, the HAProxy acme_client backend and the acme-challenge
redirect exception are skipped, as none of them are needed. Prechecks
validate the challenge type, the DNS provider and the provider
credentials. Extra lego DNS flags can be forwarded through

Add a reference CBT volume driver for vendors

Provide a minimal, fully commented reference implementation of the three
Changed Block Tracking (CBT) volume-driver methods -- create_cbt_snapshot,
get_cbt_extents (including the from_snapshot=None allocation-map path) and
delete_cbt_snapshot -- so backup and storage vendors have a neutral,
in-tree worked example to model a real driver on.

FakeCBTVolumeDriver models the backend as an in-memory map of written
blocks and computes real diffs between reference snapshots, demonstrating
the full contract: sparse full (allocation-map) backups, incremental diffs
that correctly ship a data-to-zero change, extent consolidation, idempotent
best-effort snapshot delete, and returning None as the failure signal.

This is test-only support code; it registers no new backend and ships no
data.

LVM: add Changed Block Tracking backup support for thin volumes

Implement the CBT incremental backup driver methods (create_cbt_snapshot,
get_cbt_extents, delete_cbt_snapshot) for the LVM driver when it is
configured for thin provisioning (lvm_type = thin). Reference points are
ordinary thin snapshot LVs named deterministically from the framework's
opaque reference id; the changed blocks between two of them are computed
from the thin-pool metadata using the device-mapper thin-provisioning
tools.

get_cbt_extents() runs thin_delta between the two snapshots' thin device
ids for an incremental diff, or thin_dump of the target for the full
allocation map when from_snapshot is None (making the first/full backup
sparse). A region is reported as must-ship (exists=True) when it differs
from the base -- including a change from data to zero, which thin_delta
reports as left_only. The privileged dmsetup/thin_dump/thin_delta calls
(with the pool metadata-snapshot reserve/release) run via privsep; the XML
parsing is done unprivileged and is unit-tested against real
thin-provisioning-tools output.

Thick (default) LVM is unaffected: every CBT method returns None/no-ops so
the backup framework falls back to the existing full-scan path.

Assisted-By: Claude (Opus 4.8)
Depends-On: https://review.opendev.org/c/openstack/cinder/+/990923
Change-Id: Ifcf10212cff2c46e8a9db5b06347ecf929c5a9cf
Signed-off-by: Simon Dodsley <simon@purestorage.com>

Implement the CBT incremental backup driver methods (create_cbt_snapshot,
get_cbt_extents, delete_cbt_snapshot) for the LVM driver when it is
configured for thin provisioning (lvm_type = thin). The changed blocks
between two reference snapshots are computed from the thin-pool metadata
using the device-mapper thin-provisioning tools.

get_cbt_extents() runs thin_delta between the two snapshots' thin device
ids for an incremental diff, or thin_dump of the target for the full
allocation map when from_snapshot is None (making the first/full backup
sparse). A region is reported as must-ship (exists=True) when it differs
from the base -- including a change from data to zero, which thin_delta

The snapshot identifiers get_cbt_extents()/delete_cbt_snapshot() receive

reference points. A None/absent identifier returns None rather than raising.

revisions.message:
Add worst-case Changed Block Tracking (CBT) scenario test

Add a scenario test that stresses the os-list_changed_blocks volume
action -- the first Cinder API that can return a very large payload. The
driver ships the whole changed-extent list from cinder-volume to
cinder-api over RPC, and the API windows it for the HTTP response, so a
large list exercises both the AMQP reply path and HTTP pagination (and
note that HTTP pagination does not relieve the RPC layer, which transfers
the full list on every page).

The test boots a server, attaches a volume, writes many isolated blocks
(each separated by a gap so the backend cannot consolidate them) between
two snapshots, then pages through the changed-block list asserting the
pagination contract holds and the extents are well formed. It also walks
the full allocation map (no base snapshot). It self-skips if the backend
or microversion does not support CBT (HTTP 409/406).

A ChangedBlocksClient service client issues the os-list_changed_blocks
action at microversion 3.72. A new non-voting job,
cinder-tempest-plugin-cbt-lvm-thin, runs the test against a thin LVM
backend, which implements the CBT driver API; it is non-voting during

Add a scenario test that stresses the os-list_changed_blocks volume
action -- the first Cinder API that can describe a very large number of
changed regions. The offset/length/marker/limit window is pushed all the
way down to the volume driver, so only the requested page is held in
memory and crosses Oslo RPC to cinder-api; this test verifies that path
stays correct and bounded for a large, heavily fragmented volume.

The test boots a server, attaches a volume, writes many isolated blocks
(each separated by a gap so the backend cannot consolidate them) between
two snapshots, then: pages through the changed-block list asserting the
pagination contract holds and the extents are well formed; walks the full
allocation map (no base snapshot); confirms a byte window (offset/length)
restricts the result to the requested range; and checks that paging one
extent at a time is lossless versus the larger-page walk. It self-skips
if the backend or microversion does not support CBT (HTTP 409/406).

action at microversion 3.72. A new non-voting job,

backend, which implements the CBT driver API; it is non-voting during
rollout and self-skips until the CBT framework and thin-LVM CBT driver
land.

revisions.message:
kernel: enable in-tree Intel FPGA (DFL/OPAE) support

Enable the in-tree Device Feature List (DFL) stack in both kernel-rt
and kernel-std configs so that Intel FPGA / OPAE cards (e.g. Intel PAC
N3000) are supported by the mainline drivers, without relying on the
out-of-tree opae-intel-fpga-driver DKMS package.

The OOT OPAE 2.0.1 driver mapped onto the upstream DFL framework
(drivers/fpga/dfl*) plus the MAX10 BMC, SPI, MTD and regmap pieces it
depends on. Enable the full chain as modules:

- FPGA core: FPGA, FPGA_BRIDGE, FPGA_REGION and the DFL bus
  (FPGA_DFL, FPGA_DFL_FME{,_MGR,_BRIDGE,_REGION}, FPGA_DFL_AFU,
  FPGA_DFL_PCI, FPGA_DFL_NIOS_INTEL_PAC_N3000, FPGA_M10_BMC_SEC_UPDATE)
  plus the Altera/Xilinx/Lattice/Microchip managers and bridges.
- MAX10 BMC: MFD_INTEL_M10_BMC_CORE/_SPI/_PMCI and
  SENSORS_INTEL_M10_BMC_HWMON.
- Buses/flash used by the above: REGMAP_SPI_AVMM, SPI_MEM,
  SPI_ALTERA{,_CORE,_DFL}, SPI_INTEL{,_PCI,_PLATFORM}, MTD_SPI_NOR.

The change is identical for kernel-rt and kernel-std to keep both
flavours aligned. New collateral symbols surfaced by enabling the
above (SERIAL_8250_DFL, PTP_DFL_TOD, UIO_DFL, SPI_ZYNQMP_GQSPI,
SPI_AMD) are left at their disabled defaults.

Verification:
- Build kernel and out of tree modules success for rt and std.
- Build iso success for rt and std.
- Install success onto a lab with std kernel, and can switch to rt.
- Boot up successfully in the lab; DFL/FPGA modules load and the
  FPGA devices enumerate.
- The sanity testing was run and the test results PASS.

revisions.message:
Add functional tests and Zuul job for accelerator (Cyborg)

The openstacksdk accelerator proxy has had no functional test coverage.
This means changes to the Cyborg client surface, such as removing the
v1 API from python-cyborgclient, have no CI validation against a live
service.

Add a device profile CRUD functional test exercising create, get, list,
and delete through the accelerator proxy against a devstack with Cyborg
deployed using the fake driver. Add a Zuul job definition and wire it
into the check pipeline as non-voting. Add a test_devstack.py scenario
to validate accelerator service discovery.

Assisted-by: Claude claude-opus-4-6 claude-code-2.1.198
Change-Id: Id46fb26fbdb5b4d7321ddbc9b15e679e40840df7
Signed-off-by: melanie witt <melwittt@gmail.com>

Add functional tests and Zuul job for accelerator (Cyborg)

The openstacksdk accelerator proxy has had no functional test coverage.
This means changes to the Cyborg client surface, such as removing the
v1 API from python-cyborgclient, have no CI validation against a live
service. Since python-cyborgclient's OSC plugin uses the openstacksdk
accelerator proxy directly, these tests validate the same code path
that end users exercise through the openstack CLI.

Add functional tests for all five accelerator resource types (devices,
deployables, device profiles, accelerator requests, and attributes)
against a devstack with Cyborg deployed using the fake driver. Tests
cover both admin and non-admin personas matching Cyborg's policy rules.
Add a Zuul job definition and wire it into the check pipeline as
non-voting. Add a test_devstack.py scenario to validate accelerator
service discovery.

Add functional tests and Zuul job for accelerator (Cyborg)

The openstacksdk accelerator proxy has had no functional test coverage.
This means changes to the Cyborg client surface, such as removing the
v1 API from python-cyborgclient, have no CI validation against a live
service. Since python-cyborgclient's OSC plugin uses the openstacksdk

against a devstack with Cyborg deployed using the fake driver. Tests
cover both admin and non-admin personas matching Cyborg's policy rules.

service discovery.

Cyborg API requires an internal database integer for deployable_id

volume: Add 'volume group add/remove volume' commands

Cinder supports adding and removing volumes to/from a generic volume
group via the group-update API, but python-openstackclient exposed no
command for this, forcing users to fall back to the deprecated
python-cinderclient.

Add two commands implemented on top of the openstacksdk
``update_group`` call, which is passed a comma-separated list of
volume IDs via the ``add_volumes`` / ``remove_volumes`` body fields:

  openstack volume group add volume <group> <volume> [<volume> ...]
  openstack volume group remove volume <group> <volume> [<volume> ...]

This requires the openstacksdk ``Group`` resource to declare the
``add_volumes`` and ``remove_volumes`` body fields; that fix is in
change 995940. Without it the fields are silently discarded and an
empty update request is sent to the service.

revisions.message:
Document os-list_changed_blocks in api-ref and admin guide

The changed-blocks framework added the os-list_changed_blocks volume
action (microversion 3.72) so that external backup tooling with API-only
access can query a backend's Changed Block Tracking (CBT) information.
The action was registered but not documented for API consumers: api-ref
had no entry for it, and there was no user-facing guide explaining how to
turn the returned extent map into an actual incremental copy.

Add that documentation:

* api-ref: a "List changed blocks between snapshots" action under volume
  actions, with request/response parameter definitions, request and
  response samples, the pagination/windowing parameters (offset, length,
  marker, limit / changed_blocks_next_marker), the 409 behaviour when a
  backend does not support CBT, and -- importantly for correctness -- the
  exists semantics (exists=true means allocated and must be copied,
  including a write of zeroes; exists=false means sparse and skippable).

* admin guide: "Querying changed blocks (CBT) via the API", covering the
  allocation-map (full) query, pagination, capability discovery via 409,
  and the fact that the action returns only the map of changed blocks --
  reading the changed bytes is a separate step using the normal Cinder
  data path (create volume from snapshot, attach, read the reported
  offsets), which is the sequence cinder-backup performs internally.

This is documentation only; there is no behaviour change. It depends on
the framework change that adds the action itself (and the CBT contributor
guide the admin guide cross-references).

Depends-On: https://review.opendev.org/c/openstack/cinder/+/990923
Change-Id: I59191bc0891995e3c97a518fcac91c2d745093a6
Signed-off-by: Simon Dodsley <simon@purestorage.com>

revisions.message:
Skip N3000 OPAE reset when in-tree DFL stack manages the device

On kernel 6.18 the Intel MAX10 BMC secure-update driver was migrated
from the removed /sys/class/fpga_sec_mgr subsystem to the generic
firmware-upload framework (/sys/class/firmware/<dev>/). The N3000 is
fully enumerated by the in-tree DFL/m10-bmc stack (dfl-pci ->
dfl-n3000-nios -> intel-m10-bmc-spi -> intel-m10-bmc-sec-update), but
the OPAE 'rsu bmcimg' path in the reset container targets the old ABI
and fails with exit 64 ("No compatible devices found"). Even the latest
OPAE SDK (2.14.0) does not implement rsu for the N3000 (0x0b30) over the
new sysfs ABI ("rsu not supported by this (0x8086,0x0b30)").

This blocked controller_config: the puppet N3000 reset step failed,
config-complete flags were never created, and AIO-SX stayed locked.

Detect the in-tree secure-update device and skip the legacy OPAE reset
when it is present, allowing the manifest to complete. The reset remains
in place for older kernels that still expose /sys/class/fpga_sec_mgr.

Test Plan:
  PASS: AIO-SX unlock on N3000 hardware, 6.18.15 kernel with
        CONFIG_FPGA_M10_BMC_SEC_UPDATE=m; puppet logs
        "Skipping OPAE reset" and "executed successfully".
  PASS: /sys/class/firmware/secure-update0 present after boot.

Change-Id: I93a98867c2dcb31a4fec897163e0c69893362ad1
Signed-off-by: Ionut Nechita <ionut.nechita@windriver.com>

Use max_default to make cinder reproducible

backup_workers directive uses max=processutils.get_worker_count()
which leaks the number of processors in the cinder.conf generating
machine. This makes the Cinder package non-reproducible.

If you do not know about reproducible-build, please read:
https://reproducible-builds.org/

revisions.message:
tacker-conductor with oslo.service threading

Move the tacker-conductor entry point out of `tacker.cmd.eventlet` and
select the oslo.service threading backend via `init_backend()` instead
of monkey patching the process. `oslo.service` components used by the
conductor (loopingcall, periodic_task, service.launch) are resolved
through the backend, so they switch to native threads without code
changes.

The deprecated executor argument of `get_rpc_server()` is dropped:
oslo.messaging auto-detects the executor, choosing `eventlet` when
the process is monkey patched (tacker-server) and `threading`
otherwise (tacker-conductor).

The threading backend of `oslo.service` requires the cotyledon and
futurist extras, so the requirement is bumped to
oslo.service[threading]>=4.6.0.

Depends-On: I984006c155c4f18d005611dcb7b002d1c2fb355d
Signed-off-by: Yasufumi Ogawa <yasufum.o@gmail.com>
Change-Id: Ib8d82141314e931a7e7af0ea3cb686093e2d5f4e

Remove unused eventlet code

- Remove the `tacker.agent` package. Its only module,
  agent/linux/utils.py, is not referenced anywhere in tacker.
- Remove `subprocess_popen()` and `_subprocess_setup()` from
  `tacker.common.utils`; the removed agent module was their only
  caller. This also drops the `eventlet.green` subprocess import.
- Import `sleep()` used by the cooperative readers directly from the
  time module instead of eventlet. `time.sleep(0)` yields the GIL, so
  the readers still allow other threads to be scheduled between
  chunks.
- Remove the GreenPool instantiated but never used by NfvoPlugin.

Signed-off-by: Yasufumi Ogawa <yasufum.o@gmail.com>

revisions.message:
Add --algorithm and --key-size to kube-rootca-update strategy

The kube-root-ca now defaults to ECDSA P-384 on install, but the
kube-rootca-update procedure still generates RSA 2048 with no way to
override it. Systems that upgraded from a previous release need a path
to migrate their root CA to the new default. DC deployments with N-1/N-2
subclouds need to keep RSA as an option, since the kube-root-ca can also
be used as the system local CA.

This commit adds --algorithm and --key-size CLI parameters to
sw-manager kube-rootca-update-strategy create, following the same
validation rules as the system local CA. The parameters are passed to
the sysinv API when creating certificates during orchestration.

Test Plan:
PASS: build-pkgs & build-image
PASS: Create and apply kube-rootca-update strategy on AIO-SX with
      no params, verify all certs are ECDSA P-384
PASS: Create and apply kube-rootca-update strategy on AIO-DX+Worker,
      verify compute-0 kubelet cert is ECDSA P-384
PASS: Create and apply kube-rootca-update strategy --algorithm RSA
      on AIO-SX, verify root CA is RSA 4096
PASS: Create strategy with --algorithm ECDSA --key-size 4096, verify
      rejected
PASS: Create strategy with --algorithm RSA --key-size 384, verify
      rejected
PASS: Create strategy with --key-size without --algorithm, verify
      rejected

Fix systemd presets for renamed services

Fix service name references in all preset files to
match the actual unit file names from packages:
- goenabled-worker.service -> goenabledWorker.service
- pxeboot-feed.service -> pxeboot_feed.service
- affine-platform.sh.service -> affine-platform.service

Add missing worker personality entries to aio.preset
and lowlatency.preset:
- enable worker-config-gate.service
- enable workerconfig.service

Without these entries, AIO systems fail the worker
subfunction go-enabled test (600s timeout), causing
permanent node degradation and blocking the k8s
application audit that uploads platform-integ-apps.

revisions.message:
db: Remove VPNaaS dead migration code

The ``vpn_init_ops`` module created five tables for the VPN as a
Service plugin (``vpnservices``, ``ipsecpolicies``, ``ikepolicies``,
``ipsec_site_connections``, ``ipsecpeercidrs``).  Neutron has no
models, no API extensions, and no runtime code that uses these
tables—they are exclusively consumed by the neutron-vpnaas service
plugin which now creates them itself.

Delete ``vpn_init_ops.py``, remove its import and call from
``kilo_initial.py``, and remove ``VPNAAS_TABLES`` from
``external.py``.

Depends-On: https://review.opendev.org/c/openstack/neutron-vpnaas/+/997343

revisions.message:
Replace StaticallyDelayingWrapper with futurist DelayingExecutor

nova.utils.StaticallyDelayingCancellableTaskExecutorWrapper had two
limitations: the delay was static per-executor instance (not per
submitted task), and it maintained its own scheduling loop that
duplicated logic now available in the futurist library via
futurist.DelayedExecutorMixin.

Replace it with nova.utils.DelayingExecutor, a thin subclass that
composes futurist.DelayedExecutorMixin with futurist.ThreadPoolExecutor.
Callers use submit_after(delay, fn, *args, **kwargs) to specify the
delay independently for each submitted task, eliminating the need to
instantiate a new executor per delay value.

The libvirt host driver is updated to construct DelayingExecutor
directly, and all unit tests and test fixtures are updated to use the
new class name and API.

Depends-On: https://review.opendev.org/c/openstack/futurist/+/975508
Closes-Bug: #2148910
