revisions.message:
Deploy the gateway with the quadlet framework

Stand the gateway up the way perf-tracking and wandertracks run: a
rootless quadlet pod behind socket-activated Caddy, one repo owning
the whole service. The pod manifest carries the topology (single
container, autoupdate opted in, the init annotation preserving
DEPLOYMENT.md's PID-1 requirement for the git/ssh subprocess reaping,
keep-id uid pinning); the deploy role renders the ConfigMap, the
Secret, and the Caddyfile and hands them to the shared quadlet-service
role. The profile store and the source-clone cache land in host
directories under the service user's ~/data — 0700, service-user
owned, which is exactly the mount-point contract the profile store
demands.

The Zitadel door is all-or-nothing by construction: issuer and
audience are public, reviewable job vars; the sub-to-profile mapping is
the one value that rides a Zuul secret; setting none of them (the
gate) runs bearer-only. The deploy health probe accepts the 4xx an
auth-walled front door answers with — proof the gateway, not Caddy's
502, produced the response — while the gate does the real correctness
check: mint a profile with the local admin CLI, then run an actual
streamable-http session (initialize, tools/list) through the systemd
socket and Caddy with that profile's bearer token, and assert every
container runs as the deploying user rather than namespace root.

Image jobs publish to quay.io/inaugust/opendev-mcp per DEPLOYMENT.md,
with the speculative image reaching the gate through the buildset
registry. The prod deploy is file-matched in post: routine image
rollout is podman-auto-update's job; this runs when the deployment
itself changes.

auth-walled front door answers with — proof the gateway, not Caddy's
502, produced the response — while the gate does the real correctness
check: mint a profile with the local admin CLI, then run an actual
streamable-http session (initialize, tools/list) through the systemd
socket and Caddy with that profile's bearer token, and assert every
container runs as the deploying user rather than namespace root.

Image jobs publish to quay.io/inaugust/opendev-mcp per DEPLOYMENT.md,
with the speculative image reaching the gate through the buildset
registry. The prod deploy is file-matched in post: routine image
rollout is podman-auto-update's job; this runs when the deployment
itself changes.

Also, Port to mcp 2.0

The SDK's v2 is a major rework for the 2026-07-28 protocol revision;
mcp>=1.2 now resolves to it, so move to it properly rather than pinning
backward. The gateway's surface area is small and the port is mostly
mechanical: FastMCP becomes MCPServer (mcp.server.mcpserver), transport
binding moves off Settings onto run() — which is overloaded per
transport, so stdio takes no host/port at all — and the gate client
becomes the v2 shape: headers live on an httpx2.AsyncClient handed to
streamable_http_client (which no longer takes headers=), wrapped in the
new Client.

The transport-security wiring moves with the SDK's shape: v2 takes
TransportSecuritySettings on run() and the app factories rather than
the server constructor, so the env-driven allowlist becomes a
module-level factory beside main() instead of living in build_server.
Same OPENDEV_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS contract, same both-spellings
expansion, verified live against 2.0.0: an allowlisted portless Host
passes, a rebinding attempt still gets its 421.

One change is better than mechanical: the bearer extraction moves to
ctx.headers, v2's documented accessor for the headers the transport
carried — replacing the v1 reach through request_context that was
flagged "verify against installed mcp" from the day it was written; the
one place that touches the SDK's request surface is now a documented
API. Verified by running the ported server against the real 2.0.0
in-process (v2's Client(server) transport): tools list, and an
anonymous call is refused by the auth boundary, exactly as over HTTP.

Add libaprutil1t64 1.6.4 to openstack aptly layer

The apr_memcache module in libaprutil1t64 1.6.3 (Debian Trixie)
hardcodes APR_INET (IPv4-only) when resolving the memcached server
address. On IPv6-only clusters, the memcached Kubernetes service only
has an IPv6 ClusterIP, so mod_auth_openidc fails to cache OIDC
sessions and DEX SSO returns HTTP 500.

apr-util 1.6.4 (released 2026-08-06) fixes this by using APR_UNSPEC
and adding a socket creation loop for proper address family handling:
  https://github.com/apache/apr-util/commit/9d72f3a
  https://github.com/apache/apr-util/commit/b5930d6

Debian Sid has packaged this as libaprutil1t64 1.6.4-2. Add it and
its co-installable sub-packages (libaprutil1-ldap, libaprutil1-dbd-
sqlite3) to the openstack aptly mirror layer. All three are required
because libaprutil1-ldap carries an exact-version dependency on
libaprutil1t64, and apache2 depends on libaprutil1-ldap.

The Keystone container image consumes these via its DIST_PACKAGES
and DIST_REPOS settings. Other images that enable +openstack
(stx-ceilometer, stx-openstackclient) do not depend on libaprutil
and are unaffected.

The SONAME is unchanged (libaprutil-1.so.0), dependencies are
identical to 1.6.3 — binary-compatible drop-in replacement. No IPv4
regression: APR_UNSPEC resolves identically to APR_INET on IPv4-only
clusters.

The platform ISO and host packages are not affected because the
openstack layer is excluded from the ISO build (image-layers.conf)
and the platform uses STX-built packages from deb-local-binary.

Retirement: remove these lines when Trixie ships libaprutil1t64 >=
1.6.4 natively.

revisions.message:
stx-keystone: Add openstack in DIST_REPOS

The apr_memcache module in libaprutil1t64 1.6.3 (Debian Trixie)
hardcodes APR_INET (IPv4-only) when resolving the memcached server
address. On IPv6-only clusters, mod_auth_openidc fails to cache OIDC
sessions and DEX SSO returns HTTP 500:

  oidc_cache_memcache_log_status_error: apr_memcache_getp returned
  an error: [Address family for hostname not supported]

Enable DIST_REPOS="OS +openstack" on the Keystone container image
and add libaprutil1t64, libaprutil1-ldap, and libaprutil1-dbd-
sqlite3 to DIST_PACKAGES. This pulls version 1.6.4-2 from the
openstack aptly layer, which includes the upstream IPv6 fix
(APR_UNSPEC + socket creation loop).

All three sub-packages must be listed explicitly:
  - apt does not auto-upgrade transitive dependencies
  - libaprutil1-ldap pins an exact-version dependency on
    libaprutil1t64; apache2 depends on libaprutil1-ldap

The SONAME is unchanged and dependencies are identical to 1.6.3 —
binary-compatible drop-in.

stx-openstackclient and stx-ceilometer already use "OS +openstack"
as their DIST_REPOS, establishing the pattern.

This change does not affect IPv4 or dual-stack clusters — APR_UNSPEC
resolves identically to APR_INET when IPv4 addresses exist.

revisions.message:
usm: Relocate the etcd keyspace on a simplex platform upgrade

Before the fixed-first etcd design the single etcd member ('controller')
kept its data on the DRBD-backed path /opt/etcd/db/controller.etcd. This
release founds the cluster on a fixed member ('fixed-0') backed by local
disk at /opt/etcd-fixed/db/fixed-0.etcd.

On simplex there is no second member to replicate from, so the keyspace
has to be physically relocated during the upgrade. Without it the
upgraded system comes up on an empty datastore and every Kubernetes
object is lost.

Add upgrade script 203-simplex-etcd-keyspace-migration.py, registered in
the upgrade-scripts plugin runner. It takes a snapshot of the N-1
floating data directory and restores it into the fixed member data
directory, naming the member and its cluster-host peer URL so the
resulting directory describes a single-member cluster.

The script is guarded to simplex and is a no-op elsewhere, deliberately.
Per HLD section 11.3 the fixed members on duplex are added to the still
running floating cluster with 'etcdctl member add' and populate
themselves through Raft replication; that is what
add_fixed_etcd_members_for_upgrade() does, dispatched by the periodic
membership audit on DEPLOY_STATE_ACTIVATE. Restoring a snapshot there
would seed fixed-0 as its own cluster with its own cluster ID, which
could then never join the existing one.

The script is idempotent, guarded by the marker file
/etc/platform/.etcd_upgrade_data_migrated, and fails safe: the original
floating data directory is left untouched, so a failed migration can be
retried or rolled back without data loss.

Closes-Bug: CGTS-103691
Test-Plan: WRCPPV-11160
Change-Id: Idcd5136ebc6a0ff87ef2895720ced867337749d6
Signed-off-by: bhushan.dhikale <BhushanBhaskar.Dhikale@windriver.com>

The floating instance is also taken out of service. The N-1 release ran
etcd as an SM-managed service on the DRBD-backed path; on this release a
simplex system runs only the fixed instance, so the floating service is
unmanaged by SM and disabled in systemd once the keyspace has moved.

restarted by SM, and on the next boot start against a data directory

the upgrade-scripts plugin runner. It takes a snapshot of the N-1
floating data directory and restores it into the fixed member data
directory, naming the member and its cluster-host peer URL so the
resulting directory describes a single-member cluster.

The script is guarded to simplex and is a no-op elsewhere, deliberately.
Per HLD section 11.3 the fixed members on duplex are added to the still
running floating cluster with 'etcdctl member add' and populate
themselves through Raft replication; that is what
add_fixed_etcd_members_for_upgrade() does, dispatched by the periodic
membership audit on DEPLOY_STATE_ACTIVATE. Restoring a snapshot there
would seed fixed-0 as its own cluster with its own cluster ID, which
could then never join the existing one.

The script is idempotent, guarded by the marker file
/etc/platform/.etcd_upgrade_data_migrated, and fails safe: the original
floating data directory is left untouched, so a failed migration can be
retried or rolled back without data loss.

Closes-Bug: CGTS-103691
Test-Plan: WRCPPV-11160
Depends-On: https://review.opendev.org/c/starlingx/stx-puppet/+/998118

The floating instance is also taken out of service. The N-1 release ran
etcd as an SM-managed service on the DRBD-backed path; on this release a
simplex system runs only the fixed instance, so the floating service is
unmanaged by SM and disabled in systemd once the keyspace has moved.
Left in place it would contend for the client and peer ports, be
restarted by SM, and on the next boot start against a data directory
that is no longer the cluster's.

Change-Id: Idcd5136ebc6a0ff87ef2895720ced867337749d6
Signed-off-by: bhushan.dhikale <BhushanBhaskar.Dhikale@windriver.com>

usm: relocate etcd keyspace on simplex upgrade

On simplex the etcd keyspace lives on the DRBD-backed path used by the
floating instance. The fixed-first design runs a single local-disk member
instead, so the data has to move before that member starts, or it founds an
empty cluster on the new data directory and the keyspace is lost with
nothing reporting a failure.

Relocate the keyspace during activate: mount the DRBD device if it is not
already mounted, restore the snapshot into the fixed member's data
directory, render the environment file to match, then start the member and
verify it serves the restored data before the upgrade proceeds.

The hash check is skipped on restore. The snapshot is taken from a live
member rather than written by snapshot save, so it carries no integrity
hash and etcdutl refuses it without the flag.

Duplex needs no equivalent. There the fixed members join a running cluster
and replicate through raft, so the data arrives without being moved.

Test Plan:
  PASS  simplex upgrade relocates the keyspace to the fixed member's data
        directory and the member serves it
  PASS  keys written before the upgrade read back unchanged after activate
  PASS  a second activate is a no-op
  PASS  duplex upgrade unaffected

revisions.message:
Port to mcp 2.0

The SDK's v2 is a major rework for the 2026-07-28 protocol revision;
mcp>=1.2 now resolves to it, so move to it properly rather than pinning
backward. The gateway's surface area is small and the port is mostly
mechanical: FastMCP becomes MCPServer (mcp.server.mcpserver), transport
binding moves off Settings onto run() — which is overloaded per
transport, so stdio takes no host/port at all — and the gate client
becomes the v2 shape: headers live on an httpx2.AsyncClient handed to
streamable_http_client (which no longer takes headers=), wrapped in the
new Client.

Two changes are better than mechanical. The bearer extraction moves to
ctx.headers, v2's documented accessor for the headers the transport
carried — replacing the v1 reach through request_context that was
flagged "verify against installed mcp" from the day it was written; the
one place that touches the SDK's request surface is now a documented
API. And server.py drops : v2
introspects tool signatures with eval_str=True, which evaluates
stringified annotations in module globals, where the lazily imported
Context does not exist — live annotations bind it at def time inside
build_server. That one was caught by running the ported server against
the real 2.0.0 in-process (v2's Client(server) transport): tools list,
and an anonymous call is refused by the auth boundary, exactly as over
HTTP.

Compatibility notes: a v2 server answers the legacy initialize
handshake alongside server/discover, so claude.ai and other 2025-era
clients keep connecting unchanged; the gate's client now exercises the
modern handshake. httpx stays in requirements — mcp v2 no longer
depends on it (httpx2 replaced it), but rest.py imports it in its own
right and always declared it. README's Running section also now shows
the actual console script rather than a fastmcp CLI invocation that
never matched the shipped entry point.

etcd: Configure kube-apiserver etcd endpoints for 3-member cluster

Configure kube-apiserver to use all three etcd endpoints (fixed-0,
fixed-1, floating) for duplex deployments. The etcd cluster is formed
after maintenance has completed the controller unlock via a runtime
manifest, avoiding delays to the unlock-ready flag during the initial
unlock manifest.

On simplex, only the single etcd-fixed member is used and the runtime
manifest for cluster formation is not applied.

Files:
- kubernetes.py: generate etcd hieradata with all cluster member
  endpoints for non-simplex systems
- conductor/manager.py: add _apply_etcd_runtime_manifest() to
  configure the etcd member after controller unlock, applied to
  all duplex modes (AIO-DX and Standard)

Test Plan:
PASS: AIO-DX deployment - 3 etcd endpoints configured

TODO: AIO-SX simplex - no runtime manifest applied

mariadb: Back up locally on the configured host

Kolla Ansible runs the backup container on mariadb_backup_host and
mounts the MariaDB data and backup volumes from that host.

However, the replica backup script discovers a database server through
the load balancer and may connect to a different Galera node.
Mariabackup then reads database metadata from the remote node while
reading /var/lib/mysql from the local container host. This can cause LSN
mismatches and make the backup stall.

Use the local Unix socket for both full and incremental backups. Remove
the replica-specific script so that the database connection, data files,
and backup output always belong to the host running the backup
container.

Closes-Bug: #2141558
Related: blueprint database-backup-recovery

Signed-off-by: minwooseo <alsdn1211@naver.com>

mariadb: Back up locally on the configured host

Kolla Ansible runs the backup container on mariadb_backup_host and
mounts the MariaDB data and backup volumes from that host.

However, the replica backup script discovers a database server through
the load balancer and may connect to a different Galera node.
Mariabackup then reads database metadata from the remote node while
reading /var/lib/mysql from the local container host. This can cause LSN
mismatches and make the backup stall.

Remove the replica-specific backup script and use the standard backup
script. Connection details are provided by Kolla Ansible so that the
database connection, data files, and backup output belong to the same
host.

revisions.message:
Fix multus thin-to-thick cleanup to remove config from all nodes

The existing fix for the multus thin-to-thick transition only removes
the legacy 05-multus.conf from the host where ansible runs (active
controller). On multi-node systems, the stale file persists on remote
nodes. When the thick-mode multus DaemonSet rolls out, the daemon on
those nodes picks up 05-multus.conf as clusterNetwork, causing:

- DEL path: recursive fork bomb saturating all platform CPUs
- ADD path: Unauthorized errors from stale pod-bound token

Fix by discovering all cluster nodes via kubectl and using SSH to
remove the legacy config from every node before deploying the
thick-mode DaemonSet. The cleanup is idempotent (rm -f) and
non-fatal (failed_when: false) to avoid blocking the upgrade if
a node is temporarily unreachable.

        from both controllers before thick-mode DaemonSet rollout
  PASS: K8s upgrade completes without alarm 100.101 on controller-1

  PASS: Fresh install on DX (no prior thin-mode multus) - cleanup is

revisions.message:
Revert "fix: BackupsManager.create() accept project_id keyword argument"

The project_id argument was never used by the client - create() only
sends backup_metadata in the POST body. Project scoping is handled
automatically by keystonemiddleware on the server side: the request URL
is /v2/{project_id}/backups where project_id comes from the auth token
scope, not from the request body.

The root cause was that the freezer-scheduler called
client.backups.create(metadata_doc, project_id=project_id), raising a
TypeError. The correct fix is in the scheduler (openstack/freezer):
stop passing project_id at the call site. That companion patch removes
the project_id pass-through in freezer_scheduler.py:upload_metadata().

This reverts commit 09cc1d8.

Depends-On: Iecbfc88f98984899dd7a8ac0583ea64451f31e07
Change-Id: Id169e14b686a40dadbca490fcd58f1554e1d9ab5
Signed-off-by: Jitendra Mahari <jitendra.mahari@rackspace.com>

revisions.message:
reconstructor: optionally offload EC decodes to a thread

Rebuilding a fragment runs an erasure code decode, which is CPU bound
and holds the GIL, so it stalls every other greenthread in the
reconstructor process until it finishes. Raising concurrency does not
help: the extra jobs just queue behind whichever one is decoding, so
they overlap network waits and nothing else.

With decode_offload = true each decode runs on an eventlet thread-pool
worker and the hub keeps serving other jobs while it runs. This needs a
PyECLib that releases the GIL around the liberasurecode call, otherwise
the worker thread holds the GIL just as an inline decode does and the
handoff is pure overhead. The option is ignored, with a warning at
startup, when the installed PyECLib is too old.

The check reads the version of the installed PyECLib distribution and
wants 1.9.0 or later, so the option only becomes usable once that
release is out. A checkout of PyECLib master carrying the change still
reports a pre-1.9.0 development version, and offload stays off.

There is nothing to overlap with at the default concurrency of 1, so
this only pays off for operators who have also raised concurrency.
Defaults to off.

Depends-On: Ie06eab1d5954e059a9b69b2b08b859ac1b063d06
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Change-Id: Id89a744842cd971078096fbc2d0092f3f4c7ca59
Signed-off-by: Christian Schwede <cschwede@mailbox.org>

reconstructor: optionally offload EC decodes to a thread

Rebuilding a fragment runs an erasure code decode, which is CPU bound
and holds the GIL, so it stalls every other greenthread in the
reconstructor process until it finishes. Raising concurrency does not
help: the extra jobs just queue behind whichever one is decoding, so
they overlap network waits and nothing else.

With decode_offload = true each decode runs on an eventlet thread-pool
worker and the hub keeps serving other jobs while it runs. This needs a
PyECLib that releases the GIL around the liberasurecode call, otherwise
the worker thread holds the GIL just as an inline decode does and the
handoff is pure overhead. The option is ignored, with a warning at
startup, when the installed stack is too old.

The check reads the version of the installed PyECLib distribution and
wants 1.9.0 or later, so the option only becomes usable once that
release is out. A checkout of PyECLib master carrying the change still
reports a pre-1.9.0 development version, and offload stays off. It also
checks liberasurecode, because PyECLib only drops the GIL when linked
against 1.8.0 or later and makes that same check at runtime; a wheel
from PyPI on a host with an older liberasurecode still holds it.

There is nothing to overlap with at the default concurrency of 1, so
this only pays off for operators who have also raised concurrency.
Defaults to off.

revisions.message:
Use devstack set service shutdown related config options

graceful shudown job perform the tests and many times stop
the service and wait for service to be inactive. But recently,
we have seen the failure where service did not went to inactive
and timeout happen. By checking the timeout for wait, it did not
match with what devstack set it in env and what graceful shutdown
job use to wait for status change.

devstack set service heartbeat report_internal as 120 sec
and service_down_time as 720 sec but graceful shutdown job
only wait for the 150 sec total to timeout.

THis change the test script to use the value what devstack has
set in nova conf so that we will be waiting for service down
status as nova heartbeat is configured.

Closes-Bug: #2163448

Change-Id: Icfa6009be5b70b4cb46618814f0f01add5298493
Signed-off-by: Ghanshyam Maan <gmaan@ghanshyammann.com>

Use service shutdown related config options in nova-graceful-shutdown

nova-graceful-shutdown job's tests stop the service and wait for service
status to be inactive. But recently, we have seen the failure where service
did not went to inactive and timeout happen. Nova service status update depends
on the heartbeat controlled by the two config option (report_interval,
service_down_time). But test scripts do not consider those config option
and timeout on service inactive status change before service status is updated.
Devstack set service heartbeat report_internal as 120 sec and service_down_time
as 720 sec but graceful shutdown job only wait for the 150 sec.

This change set those config option value in job definition and use the same in
test script.

Closes-Bug: #2163448

Change-Id: Icfa6009be5b70b4cb46618814f0f01add5298493
Signed-off-by: Ghanshyam Maan <gmaan@ghanshyammann.com>

subject: Use service shutdown related config options in nova-graceful-shutdown

revisions.message:
Fix 'swfit' typo in backup storage driver default

BuiltInstanceTasks.create_backup defaults the storage driver to the
misspelled string 'swfit' when backup_info lacks a 'storage_driver'
key. 'swfit' matches neither "cinder" nor 'swift', so the taskmanager
casts the backup to the guest without injecting swift_url. Since
804f960b ("Use pre-auth Swift client, drop Keystone re-auth") the
guest agent hard-requires swift_url and rejects such a request with
"Missing swift_url in backup metadata".

The broken default is hard to reach in practice: both in-tree
producers of backup_info always set storage_driver (falling back to
CONF.storage_strategy), so hitting it requires either a mixed-version
rolling upgrade — a trove-api still running code from before e4113c55
("Support new storage driver for backup objects", which introduced
both the field and this typo) casting create_backup to a current
taskmanager, backup_info being a plain dict with no versioned schema
— or an out-of-tree caller of the taskmanager RPC API. On the stable
branches that carry the typo it is currently harmless, because the
guest-side swift_url requirement only exists on master.

Fix the default and add regression coverage for
BuiltInstanceTasks.create_backup, which previously had no tests.

branches that carry the typo it is currently harmless, because the
guest-side swift_url requirement only exists on master.

revisions.message:
etcd: move the control plane onto the load balancer during activate

Balancing the HAProxy backends achieves nothing while controlPlaneEndpoint
still names the cluster-host floating address with no port: kubeadm resolves
a portless endpoint through localAPIEndpoint.bindPort, so every kubelet,
kube-proxy, controller manager, scheduler and admin.conf in the cluster
holds 16443 and reaches whichever API server happens to hold the floating
address. An upgrade that forms the etcd cluster but leaves the endpoint
where it was has not delivered PR.952.02.

Activate is the moment for it. Every host is running the new load by then
and HAProxy is serving on all of them, which the helper insists on before it
touches anything. Simplex is skipped, matching the gate sysinv applies at
unlock -- one API server, nothing to balance.

A failure to move the endpoint is logged rather than raised. The etcd
cluster is already formed at that point and is what the rest of the
deployment depends on; an endpoint that has not moved leaves the cluster
working exactly as it did before, and the helper can be run again by hand.

The endpoint is deliberately not reverted on activate-rollback. The release
being rolled back to already serves 6443 -- k8s-frontend-internal is present
in it, with a single backend -- so kubeconfigs left naming the balancer keep
working there. Reverting would mean reaching every worker to rewrite a file
that activate-rollback has no way to reach, in order to move traffic off an
endpoint that is serving it correctly. --revert stays available for an
operator who wants the older layout back.

Test Plan:
PASS: AIO-DX 26.03 -> 26.10, after "software deploy activate" all five
      kubeconfigs name <cluster-floating>:6443 and both haproxy backends
      take connections
PASS: Standard 2+2, same, verified from a worker with "kubectl get nodes"
PASS: AIO-SX activate leaves the endpoint alone
PASS: activate re-run is a no-op on the endpoint
PASS: HAProxy stopped at activate time -- etcd work still succeeds, endpoint
      is not moved, warning names the helper to re-run
PASS: "software deploy activate-rollback" then host-rollback per the USM Eng
      guide order; cluster reachable throughout on the 26.03 load

Story: 2010302
Change-Id: I02e57800032a52ea03792cc2eb663a5db1b47b6a
Signed-off-by: Mahesh S <mahesh.saptasagar@windriver.com>

NetApp ONTAP REST: restore snapshot-dir fallback for CG clones

Restores two code paths dropped when patch 993363 was split to remove
its bug-fix portion:

* nfs_cmode.py stopped passing source_snapshot to clone_file(), so NFS
  CG-snapshot clones silently sourced from the live file instead of
  the snapshot.
* client_cmode_rest.py's clone_lun()/clone_file() lost the
  snapshot_directory_access_enabled check and private-CLI fallback, so
  clones failed outright when that FlexVol setting is False.

Restores get_volume_snapshot_dir_access(), _clone_via_private_cli(),
_clone_lun_via_private_cli(), _check_lun_visible(), the fallback
branching in clone_lun()/clone_file(), and their unit tests.

Verified live on a real ONTAP cluster: iSCSI and NFS CG-snapshot clones
now succeed with snapshot_directory_access_enabled both True and
False, and the NFS clone log shows the real snapshot id instead of
None.

revisions.message:
etcd: add certificate reissue and fix member-add guard for SX-to-DX

The simplex-to-duplex migration path fails on the first duplex unlock
because of two issues in the etcd puppet code:

1. Certificate SAN mismatch: At simplex bootstrap the etcd server
   certificate only carries the cluster-host floating address in its
   Subject Alternative Name set. After conversion the membership class
   rewrites etcd-fixed to bind the controller-0 unit address, and the
   TLS handshake fails because the certificate does not cover it.

   Fix: add platform::etcd::certificates, a puppet class that calls
   etcd_duplex_migration.py --certificates to reissue the certificate
   with the full SAN set (floating + both unit addresses + loopback).
   The class is ordered after platform::network writes /etc/hosts and
   before platform::etcd::membership restarts etcd-fixed. An unless
   guard makes it a no-op when the SAN set is already correct (fresh
   duplex bootstrap).

2. Member-add unless guard: The migration playbook registers the
   floating etcd member as a learner before the unlock. At unlock
   puppet tries to add it again. The unless guard greps for the member
   name ('controller'), but an unstarted learner has an empty name
   field in 'etcdctl member list' output -- only the peer URL is
   present. The grep fails, puppet runs the add, etcd returns "Peer
   URLs already exists", and controllerconfig fails.

   Fix: extend the unless guard to also match the floating peer URL
   so it catches both started (by name) and unstarted (by URL) members.

Test Plan:
- AIO-SX to AIO-DX migration with etcd-ha-controlplane topic
- Verified controller-0 boots into duplex mode after unlock
- Verified etcd cluster has 2 members (fixed-0 + controller/floating)
- Verified fresh duplex bootstrap is unaffected (certificates class skips)

Change-Id: I40509e4a6ad66165366208c467a4ce331e9f1cf0
Signed-off-by: Mohammad Adnan Nasim <MohammadAdnan.Nasim@windriver.com>

because of two issues in the etcd puppet code:

   certificate only carries the cluster-host floating address in its
   Subject Alternative Name set. After conversion the membership class
   rewrites etcd-fixed to bind the controller-0 unit address, and the
   TLS handshake fails because the certificate does not cover it.

   etcd_duplex_migration.py --certificates to reissue the certificate
   with the full SAN set (floating + both unit addresses + loopback).
   The class is ordered after platform::network writes /etc/hosts and
   before platform::etcd::membership restarts etcd-fixed. An unless
   guard makes it a no-op when the SAN set is already correct (fresh
   duplex bootstrap).

   field in 'etcdctl member list' output -- only the peer URL is
   present. The grep fails, puppet runs the add, etcd returns "Peer
   URLs already exists", and controllerconfig fails.

   Fix: extend the unless guard to also match the floating peer URL
   so it catches both started (by name) and unstarted (by URL) members.

revisions.message:
Allow shrinking a segment range to an allocated boundary

Updating a network segment range to reduce its minimum or maximum was
rejected as referenced by a tenant network even when every allocated
segment still fell within the requested new range. The guard against
stranding allocated segments used inclusive comparisons (>= and <=),
so a new boundary that landed exactly on the lowest or highest
allocated segment was wrongly treated as impacting them.

Use strict comparisons so the update is only blocked when the new
minimum rises above the lowest allocated segment or the new maximum
drops below the highest allocated segment.

Depends-On: https://review.opendev.org/c/openstack/neutron-tempest-plugin/+/1000364
Closes-Bug: #2161678
Assisted-By: Claude Opus 4.8
Change-Id: Ibc51c722669f3ea9b16d6821554d92fcb5f924c3
Signed-off-by: Doug Goldstein <cardoe@cardoe.com>
(cherry picked from commit 0ea814f6a41d6fa39fad6a68d57af68bbe89a589)

revisions.message:
WIP: Add REDIRECT_SCHEME L7 policy action

The current L7 policy actions only support redirecting to a
hardcoded URL or path prefix. This means HTTP requests cannot be
upgraded to HTTPS in place while preserving the full request path
and query parameters, and it does not work with wildcard
certificate deployments where the target host is not known ahead
of time.

Add a new REDIRECT_SCHEME L7 policy action that redirects the
request to the same host, path, and query parameters with the
scheme changed to HTTPS, using HAProxy's "redirect scheme https"
directive. This adds a new l7policy_action lookup table entry via
a database migration and bumps the API to microversion 2.31.

This depends on the REDIRECT_SCHEME action constant being added to
octavia-lib.

Closes-Bug: #2060539

Change-Id: I674e72adc3e180fcb1c2fbb55bc89c4a9c013a9c

revisions.message:
Add Stripe billing foundation: schema, entitlements, secrets wiring

Task S2 (doc/plans/stripe-billing.md): lands the plumbing S3
(checkout/portal/status) and S4 (webhook) build on, with zero
observable behavior change for today's deployment.

Schema: users.stripe_customer_id (nullable, unique), added to the
existing table via the same dialect-safe idempotent-ALTER mechanism
task E1a introduced for identities.git_fullname/git_email
(ensure_user_billing_columns, wired into opendev-mcp-init beside
ensure_identity_git_columns) -- the unique constraint itself only
applies to a fresh create_all, not a retrofitted ALTER, a deliberate
gap documented on that function. Two new tables via create_all:
billing_subscriptions (one row per user, upserted only by S4's
webhook handlers) and billing_events (processed Stripe event ids, the
webhook's idempotency guard). billing_subscriptions carries no
ordering/version column -- S4's write path is trigger-and-reconcile
(materialize from an authoritative Subscription refetch on every
status-changing event, per the plan's "Webhook: idempotency and
reconciliation" section), so there is nothing here for a webhook
write to compare against; nothing writes this table yet, S4 is the
first writer, same as every other webhook-owned column here.

opendev_mcp/billing.py: env-driven BillingConfig (API key, webhook
secret, Pro Price ids, Pro caps) and an injectable StripeClient seam
(LazyStripeClient/build_stripe_client) using the SDK's
client-instance pattern exclusively -- never the deprecated
module-global stripe.api_key -- pinned to stripe_version
"2026-07-29.dahlia" on every constructed client. No endpoints yet.

opendev_mcp/entitlements.py: entitlements_for(user_or_user_id,
session) -> Entitlements(plan_key, max_identities,
max_tokens_per_identity), reading billing_subscriptions
(active/trialing/past_due status on a price id this deployment
recognizes as Pro; everything else, including an empty table, is
Free). past_due grants Pro, reconciled here against the amended
plan's now-explicit status-to-plan mapping: Smart Retries keeps a
failed-payment subscription in past_due for days before Stripe gives
up, and downgrading on the first failed charge would defeat the point
of Smart Retries -- only the actual final-lapse statuses
(canceled/unpaid/incomplete_expired/incomplete) resolve to Free. Free
defaults are byte-for-byte the old OPENDEV_MCP_MAX_IDENTITIES_PER_USER
/OPENDEV_MCP_MAX_TOKENS_PER_IDENTITY env reads, moved here from
identities_api.py/tokens_api.py's own per-router helpers -- both
routers now call the resolver at their cap chokepoints instead,
threading the console door's existing session_factory through their
router builders.

Secrets: investigated inaugust/inaugust.com's quadlet-service role
before reaching for the plan's env-file fallback, and found a
first-class mechanism already there -- quadlet_secrets writes
Kubernetes Secret YAML (0600, no_log) and loads it into podman's own
secret store via `podman kube play` before the pod restarts, resolved
by the pod manifest via envFrom.secretRef with no value ever written
into the manifest. Used it directly: stripe-secret.yaml.j2 (blank
defaults, no real or placeholder values), wired into the deploy
role's quadlet_secrets and the gateway container's envFrom
unconditionally. The env-file fallback is therefore not implemented.
Non-secret billing vars (Price ids, Pro caps) ride the existing
opendev-mcp-env ConfigMap.

DEPLOYMENT.md gets a "Billing (Stripe)" section (env vars, the
secrets mechanism, operator action, "endpoints land in later tasks")
and README.rst a one-line pointer.

Reconciled against the plan commit's PS1-review-driven amendment
(org.zuul-ci.change=1001261 PS1 comments): moved past_due from
entitlements.py's non-entitling set into its entitling set (plus a
dedicated regression test and a loop test over every entitling
status) so this resolver matches the plan's now-explicit
status-to-plan mapping before S4 has to build on it.

Reconciled again against the plan commit's PS2-review-driven amendment
(org.zuul-ci.change=1001261 PS2 comments): the plan's ordering design
changed from a last_event_created timestamp comparison to
trigger-and-reconcile (an authoritative Subscription refetch per
status-changing event, since `created` timestamps can't establish a
total order and a Subscription's own `created` was never a valid
version signal to begin with) -- this commit's prior revision had
already landed billing_subscriptions.last_event_created and its
model/table tests for the old design; both are removed here, along
with the Integer import that column was the only user of, and every
docstring cross-reference to the plan's now-renamed "Webhook:
idempotency and reconciliation" section is updated to match. Nothing
else in this schema/resolver depends on the column, so nothing else
changes.

Reconciled a third time against the plan commit's PS3-review-driven
amendment (org.zuul-ci.change=1001261 PS3 comments): the plan's
"Checkout: customer and session concurrency" section gained a
billing_checkout_attempts table (a per-user Checkout Session
"generation" that /checkout converges concurrent/retried callers onto
via a lifecycle-scoped Stripe idempotency key -- Stripe's own
idempotency layer, not this database, does the actual converging;
this table only makes sure every racing caller resolves the same key)
-- this commit adds that table (models.py's BillingCheckoutAttempt,
user_id PRIMARY KEY straight to users.id rather than a separate
surrogate id, since there is at most one live in-flight-checkout row
per user; generation integer defaulting to 1; nullable, deliberately
NOT unique session_id, since every concurrent caller within one
generation legitimately records the identical Stripe session id) plus
its model/table tests, matching this module's existing
BillingSubscription/BillingEvent docstring and test conventions
(including the Integer import the new generation column needs).
Nothing reads or writes this table yet -- task S3 is the first
reader/writer, same as billing_subscriptions/billing_events above.
Nothing else in this commit changes; task S3/S4 own the actual
CAS-insert-or-read, idempotency-key, and rotation logic the plan's
amended section specifies.

tox -e pep8,py3 green (901 tests, was 896); `cd web && npm run ci` green
and untouched.

Reconciled a fourth time against the plan commit's PS4-review-driven
amendment (org.zuul-ci.change=1001261 PS4 comments): the plan's
pending-attempt lifecycle gained a terminal_at marker (completion no
longer deletes/resets the attempt row -- generation must survive,
durable and monotonic, for a later legitimate post-cancellation
checkout to rotate forward from, so a fresh Stripe idempotency key is
guaranteed even within Stripe's ~24h retention window) --
BillingCheckoutAttempt gains terminal_at: Mapped[datetime.datetime |
None], same nullable single-use-marker shape this module already uses
for OAuthCode.used_at/Connection.revoked_at, set once a generation's
Session is observed complete-and-reconciled WITHOUT touching
generation/session_id (marking terminal is deliberately not the same
operation as rotating). Model/table tests added for the new column
(nullable, no default) plus a construction test proving it is settable
independently of generation/session_id. Nothing else in this commit
changes; task S3 owns the actual authoritative-Session-retrieve gate
and rotation logic the plan's amended section specifies.

Addresses a review finding on patch set 1 of this commit's own change
(1001262): ensure_user_billing_columns previously added
users.stripe_customer_id without ever retrofitting its UNIQUE
constraint on an upgraded table, leaving upgraded deployments
(including production) permanently on a weaker schema than a fresh
create_all -- a real gap, since a Stripe customer id is a billing/
account-ownership boundary, not an approximate quota. Verified
directly against drizzled/sql_yacc.yy in opendev.org/drizzle/drizzle
(branch main) rather than guessing: its `create` production carries a
standalone `CREATE [UNIQUE] INDEX ident ON table_ident (...)`
alternative, distinct from `CREATE TABLE`, with no `IF NOT EXISTS`
clause (matching this module's existing check-then-DDL idempotency
discipline). Chosen over the grammar-supported `ALTER TABLE ... ADD
UNIQUE` specifically because `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` is the one DDL
shape that works identically across Drizzle, real MySQL, AND the unit
suite's own SQLite backend, which has no `ALTER TABLE ... ADD
CONSTRAINT` at all. ensure_user_billing_columns now also checks for an
index covering stripe_customer_id (mysql/Drizzle family: a raw `SHOW
INDEXES FROM users`, read positionally at index 4 -- the one position
that agrees between MySQL's and Drizzle's differently-shaped output,
since Drizzle's own SHOW_INDEXES data-dictionary table is narrower and
has the OPPOSITE polarity at index 1 from MySQL's Non_unique; every
other dialect: Inspector.get_unique_constraints unioned with
Inspector.get_indexes, since this migration's own CREATE UNIQUE INDEX
reflects back via the latter, not the former, on SQLite) and issues
the CREATE UNIQUE INDEX only when missing. New test coverage: two
sqlite-backed functional tests (adds the index to a pre-S2 table and
proves it actually enforces the invariant via a duplicate-insert
IntegrityError; idempotent on a second call) plus a fresh-create_all
regression test proving the ORM's own inline UNIQUE constraint is
recognized and never gets a redundant index layered on top, and three
mysql-dialect fake-harness tests (adds the index when SHOW INDEXES
reports none covering the column; idempotent when it does; and a
PS6-style regression test pinning that Inspector.get_unique_constraints
is never called for the mysql/Drizzle family, mirroring the existing
get_columns restriction). The model's own User.stripe_customer_id
docstring and this function's docstring are both rewritten to match --
there is no longer a documented gap on the ALTER path.

tox -e pep8,py3 green (909 tests, was 901 before this round of fixes);
`cd web && npm run ci` green and untouched.

revisions.message:
Run the Android contract suite in the integration job

The one end-to-end job grows its fourth suite: the Android app's
contract tests, run through the app's real network stack (Retrofit,
Moshi, the WanderTracksApi interface, X-API-Key auth) against the
same deployed front door the Python contract suite exercises. The
sharpest thing this buys is verification of the status-code
semantics the app's sync engine and recovery path were written
against — stop-after-stop answering 404/409 — which until now
existed only as an assumption inside mocked unit tests.

The android repo's rootless toolchain role is composed the way the
service repos' deploy roles already are; rootless matters because
this play runs after the parent's revoke-sudo, so the toolchain
install happens in run rather than needing a privileged pre-run.
The gradle invocation is the same one a developer runs, filtered to
the contract package; WANDERTRACKS_CONTRACT_API_URL un-gates tests
that are skipped everywhere else.

A third developer-mode key joins the gate deployment: distinct key,
distinct user, so the Android suite's tracks and visits are
invisible to both Python suites sharing the deployment (keys differ
within their first 8 characters, which is where the auth handler
derives the user).

The job timeout goes to 3600: the toolchain download plus gradle's
first-use dependency resolution add real minutes atop the deploy.

revisions.message:
Pin the style builder to the API repo's vendored JSON

Phase 2 of doc/plans/mapstyle-architecture.md (in the API repo)
starts here: before the basemap catalog flips to consuming the
styles the API serves and the TypeScript builders are deleted, prove
the handoff loses nothing.

The new studio test renders every BASEMAP_OPTIONS entry through
getMapStyle() with the {{ESRI_API_TOKEN}} placeholder - exactly how
the one-time exporter generated the vendored files - and deep-
compares the result against wandertracks/mapstyles/<id>.json in the
API repo, plus checks the two sides agree on which basemaps exist.
Comparison is structural rather than textual on purpose: the
vendored files are pretty-printed for human editing while the
builder output is compact, and formatting is not style.

The API checkout is found alongside this repo - the layout Zuul's
required-projects produces and the natural developer layout - or via
WANDERTRACKS_API_SRC. The studio-test job now declares
wandertracks/wandertracks in required-projects, so CI always runs
the comparison (a lone local checkout skips with a note), and
Depends-On gates cross-repo style edits: vendored JSON and builder
must land together or fail together.

Once the flip lands and the builders are deleted, this test is
deleted with them; its whole job is proving the migration.

Depends-On: https://review.opendev.org/c/wandertracks/wandertracks/+/1001388
Change-Id: Ie11157c1945895af512b6ecd8530e5df35f76c7f

revisions.message:
Add the gerrit-stack-walk skill

Packages the review-walk process this project has itself been built
with (~40 review rounds) into a distributable Claude Code skill, so a
session picks up the process automatically instead of re-deriving it
each time.

- skills/gerrit-stack-walk/SKILL.md: the two-pass discipline (review
  bottom-up, then CI bottom-up) — one change pushed at a time with
  fresh shas, fixes made in the owning commit via a splice
  (checkout/fix/git add <paths>/amend/rebase --onto, always re-running
  tests even on a conflict-free rebase), Change-Id preserved verbatim,
  TRIVIAL_REBASE vote-copy behavior explained, stale-patchset recovery
  via the Zuul status API + recheck, and a harness-degrading "Waiting"
  section (background Monitor + watch-change.sh in Claude Code, manual
  gerrit_fetch_change polling elsewhere) — plus a tool reference table
  and a pitfalls list. Distilled from doc/plans/web-console.md's and
  (on a sibling branch) stripe-billing.md's "one gate-green commit per
  task" task-breakdown discipline and the full 12-tool gateway surface
  in opendev_mcp/server.py, including the gerrit_fetch_comments tool
  this skill leans on for reading inline findings.
- skills/gerrit-stack-walk/scripts/watch-change.sh: the poller the
  skill's "Waiting" section calls out. Takes a message-count baseline
  on its own first poll (documented race: start it, or otherwise
  snapshot the count, before pushing — not after), polls
  changes/{N}/detail, strips the )]}' XSSI guard, filters messages by
  author against WATCH_IGNORE_AUTHORS (default "Zuul,<this repo's git
  identity>"), separately catches Zuul "Build failed"/"Merge Failed"
  text even though Zuul is itself in the default ignore list, and
  prints current Code-Review votes alongside the triggering message(s)
  before exiting 0. Shellcheck-clean, bash -n clean, executable bit
  set; exercised end-to-end against a throwaway local HTTP fixture
  serving Gerrit-shaped JSON (baseline capture, ignored-author
  filtering, and the Zuul-failure carve-out all verified).
- skills/README.rst: what this directory is (the future skill://
  serving root for an MCP skills-provider task) and how to add a skill.
- .claude/skills/gerrit-stack-walk -> ../../skills/gerrit-stack-walk:
  symlink so Claude Code sessions in this checkout auto-load the
  skill. Verified two ways: (1) git tracks it as a real symlink blob
  (mode 120000) in this repo (core.symlinks unset, i.e. the platform
  default of following/storing symlinks applies) — the same idiom
  wandertracks already uses for its CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md; (2)
  Claude Code's own skills documentation confirms project skill
  discovery follows a symlinked skill directory and reads SKILL.md
  from its target, deduplicating by target when reachable via more
  than one path. No pointer-file fallback was needed.

tox -e pep8,py3: both pass. ruff only lints opendev_mcp/tests, so it
doesn't see the new skill files; py3 stays at 848 tests (unchanged —
no Python source touched). web/ untouched.

Consume the served basemap styles; delete the builders

The WanderTracks basemap styles are now vendored JSON in the API repo,
served at /api/v1/styles/<id>.json with the Esri token substituted
server-side (doc/plans/mapstyle-architecture.md there, Phase 2). The
parity suite proved the served JSON structurally identical to what the
builders here produce, so the builders go:

- mapstyle.ts loses getMapStyle and the five per-basemap builders;
  transportLayers, waterLayers, parkLayers and labelLayers (~5,000
  lines of literal layer specs) are deleted outright. What remains is
  what was never style data: BASEMAP_OPTIONS (catalog metadata the
  selector renders) and the track-grouping styling machinery, which
  stays authoritative until plan Phases 4/6 move it server-side.
- resolveBasemapStyle and the editor registry's WanderTracks entries
  resolve to style URLs from the new map/style-urls.ts - the same
  string-URL shape every third-party basemap already uses, so the
  StyleManager and WanderTracksMap paths need no changes. The base
  moves with api.setApiBaseUrl for preview environments; unlike the
  retired token there is no already-built-style rebuild problem,
  because a URL resolves when MapLibre fetches it.
- The detail maps (trip detail, public trip, live recording, dive
  detail, flight repair) merged boundary lines into an inline spec at
  construction, so they gain fetchDetailMapStyle(): fetch the served
  basemap, merge boundaries, then construct - with a cancellation
  guard for teardowns that race the fetch, and an empty-style
  fail-soft so a backendless dev server still renders the caller's
  own layers.

  token-rotation rebuild in editor-basemap.ts and the config plumbing

  field itself stays until the Android app stops reading it (plan
  Phase 5).

  deleted with the code they tested; basemap-catalog.test.ts now pins
  the URL resolution. mapstyle-parity.test.ts is deleted too, its job
  done - it existed to prove this change loses nothing.

revisions.message:
Keep the unscoped credential of a federated plugin

A federated plugin gets an unscoped token and then rescopes it. Keep
that unscoped token in the keyring under its own key, so that one
authentication serves every scope rather than one each. For an
interactive flow that is the difference between one login and several.

It is loaded whether or not a scoped token was cached with it, since
the federated plugins do not support the scoped cache at all, and is
only stored where the plugin reports that authenticating needs the
user.

revisions.message:
etcd: issue per-member certificates instead of one shared cert

POC -- DO NOT MERGE. Alternative to the shared multi-SAN certificate used by
998137/998139, raised so the two models can be compared on a lab before a
decision is taken. Not part of the etcd-ha-controlplane topic and carries no
Depends-On into that stack.

Today every etcd member presents the same /etc/etcd/etcd-server.crt for both
client and peer TLS, and multi-member coverage comes from stacking every
address into that one certificate's SAN list. ETCD_PEER_CLIENT_CERT_AUTH is
enabled but cannot distinguish one member from another, because there is only
one identity to present; compromise of the key exposes the whole cluster, and
rotation is all or nothing.

Issue a key pair per member instead. Each certificate's common name carries the
etcd member name and its SAN covers only the address that member binds, so peer
authentication can assert which member is connecting rather than only that the
certificate was signed by our CA.

controller-1's key pair is deliberately not generated here. It is created on
controller-1 at unlock so the private key never crosses a host boundary, which
is the property that makes per-member keys worth having. Bootstrap therefore
issues fixed-0 and the floating member only.

The apiserver client certificate keeps the full address set. SANs on a client
certificate do not authorise it -- the server matches common name and extended
key usage -- so narrowing it belongs in a separate change if wanted at all.

Test Plan:
  PASS  bootstrap issues etcd-fixed-0 and etcd-server with disjoint SANs
  PASS  etcd-fixed-0 CN is fixed-0, SAN is the controller-0 cluster-host address
  PASS  simplex bootstrap unaffected, no controller-1 material generated
  TODO  duplex: controller-1 self-issues fixed-1 at unlock
  TODO  peer authentication rejects a member presenting another member's cert

revisions.message:
sysinv: renew per-member etcd certificates on their own host

POC -- DO NOT MERGE. Completes the per-member certificate set with
ansible-playbooks 1001457 (issue at bootstrap) and stx-puppet 1001458 (consume
on the fixed members). Raised so the per-member and shared multi-SAN models can
be compared on a lab before a decision is taken. Not part of the
etcd-ha-controlplane topic and carries no Depends-On into that stack.

Renewal is the half that decides whether per-member certificates survive
contact with a real system: certificates that are issued once and then renewed
back into a shared identity are worse than not splitting them at all.

Each controller renews only its own fixed member. The peer renews its own, so
there is nothing to do for it here. The floating certificate keeps its shared
handling because the floating member genuinely can run on either controller,
but its SAN set narrows to the floating address and the loopbacks now that the
unit addresses are carried by the per-member certificates.

There is deliberately no copy of the member key into ${CONFIG_PATH}/etcd. The
floating pair is replicated to the standby because it has to be; a fixed
member's key must not leave its host, and replicating it would quietly undo
the whole point.

Renewal is skipped with a log line if no per-member certificate is present, so
a system still on the shared model is unaffected.

Test Plan:
  TODO  duplex: each controller renews only its own member, CN preserved
  TODO  etcd accepts renewed per-member certs without disruption
  TODO  no member key appears under ${CONFIG_PATH}/etcd after renewal
  TODO  a shared-model system skips the new block cleanly
  TODO  sysinv-tox-flake8, -pylint, -py39, -bandit

revisions.message:
sysinv: apply the control-plane endpoint manifest after unlock

Move controlPlaneEndpoint from the kube-apiserver port onto the HAProxy
load balancer after unlock. Bootstrap points it at kube-apiserver directly
because HAProxy is configured by the unlock manifest and started by Service
Manager, so nothing listens on :6443 while kubeadm init runs.

Apply it from iplatform_update_by_ihost() on the first-report-available
path, immediately after the etcd runtime manifest. The same guards apply:
controller personality, non-simplex, initial config complete.

This also covers the other lifecycle paths without a separate hook:
- simplex-to-duplex: the script returns early on simplex, picks up on
  the first unlock as duplex
- upgrade/rollback: each unlock re-applies, no-op when already correct
- restore: reconciles from whatever the backup captured

revisions.message:
Support pushing to registered Gerrit servers

M5 of the multi-Gerrit series: extend the workspace/push layer
(opendev_mcp/patch.py) so create_change/revise_change/replace_change
can push against any registered (non-default) Gerrit server, not just
the identity's default one.

- PushTarget (patch.py) is the lightweight, non-I/O descriptor the
  push functions now accept alongside GerritAccount; push_target_for()
  projects a ProfileStore.resolve_gerrit_server() result onto it. The
  default-server path (GerritAccount + workspace.ensure_source_clone)
  is completely untouched.
- SSH mode: the remote embeds the network-boundary-vetted IP
  (resolve_public_host, resolved once per push and reused throughout —
  never re-resolved mid-push), with -o HostKeyAlias=<host[:port]> so
  known_hosts verification stays keyed by hostname. known_hosts content
  comes from the gerrit_servers row's pinned ssh_host_keys, written to
  a per-invocation 0600 file; a NULL ssh_host_keys refuses the push
  with a clear "refresh host keys" error (no TOFU at push time).
- HTTP mode: the remote embeds the username only; the password travels
  via a GIT_ASKPASS helper (a static, secret-free 0700 script per
  invocation) reading OPENDEV_MCP_GIT_USERNAME/PASSWORD from the
  subprocess env — never argv, the URL, or git config. Every
  network-touching git call is pinned via http.curloptResolve, applied
  through GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_0/VALUE_0 env vars rather than an argv
  -c flag so it also reaches git-review's own internal `git push`
  subprocess. A git-version gate refuses HTTP-mode pushes on a git
  older than 2.31 (curloptResolve support), since an old git would
  silently ignore the pin and connect unpinned.
- Per-server git_fullname/git_email (already resolved by
  ResolvedGerritServer) thread through the existing identity-env
  mechanism; _git_identity_env now accepts either account-ish type.
- known_hosts_host_field is lifted from identities_api.py into
  accounts.py (shared, pure) so both the M4 keyscan-pinning path and
  this module's ssh pinning use one definition.
- identities_api.py's POST .../gerrit-servers now runs a real soft SSH
  check (patch.soft_ssh_check) instead of always reporting "skipped",
  reusing the same pinned-connection plumbing and the address the
  keyscan step already vetted; response shape is unchanged
  ("ok" | "failed: <category>" | "skipped").

Tests: unit coverage for remote URL construction (both modes, IPv6),
GIT_SSH_COMMAND/GIT_ASKPASS/curloptResolve construction, askpass
execution (both prompts), file permissions (0600/0700), the
DNS-rebinding-defense "single resolution reused for the whole push"
behavior, netpolicy refusal propagation, missing-credential/host-key
errors, scratch-directory cleanup (including on early failure), a
password leak-hunt across every captured argv/env, per-server git
identity threading, the git-version gate, and soft_ssh_check's
ok/failed-category/skipped outcomes. tox -e pep8 and tox -e py3 pass
(1696 tests).

Round-9 fix: the next deterministic Zuul failure, one layer deeper
than the round-6/7 ones (Archon's CI diagnosis on 1001734 PS3): the
multi-Gerrit setup, credential verification, and reads all worked --
the first HTTP-mode gerrit_create_change then failed cloning
https://gate-gerrit/a/gate/sandbox/ with git/libcurl rejecting the
fixture certificate ("certificate signer not trusted", using
/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt, git's OWN default bundle).
httpx (this module's own REST clients, and the console door's OIDC
discovery) honors SSL_CERT_FILE natively for its trust store, but
git's own HTTPS transport (libcurl) does not -- it needs
GIT_SSL_CAINFO (env) or http.sslCAInfo (config) to trust anything
beyond its compiled-in default, and _env_for_target (which owns the
git subprocess env construction for HTTP-mode targets) never threaded
SSL_CERT_FILE through to it.

Fixed generically, not as gate-only plumbing: when the gateway
process's own environment carries SSL_CERT_FILE, _env_for_target now
also sets GIT_SSL_CAINFO to that same path for HTTP-mode targets,
unless GIT_SSL_CAINFO is already present in the process env (an
operator who set it explicitly -- deliberately a different trust
store just for git -- wins over the inference). Documented in the
function's own docstring as the general production behavior it is:
an operator pointing the whole gateway at a private-CA Gerrit via
SSL_CERT_FILE now gets git trusting the same store httpx already
does, not just REST calls. Checked DEPLOYMENT.md/README.rst/doc/ for
any existing SSL_CERT_FILE documentation to extend with a one-line
git-follows-it-too note -- none exists (SSL_CERT_FILE is currently
gate-only plumbing, never operator-documented), so no doc section was
invented.

Tests: unit coverage for remote URL construction (both modes, IPv6),
GIT_SSH_COMMAND/GIT_ASKPASS/curloptResolve construction, askpass
execution (both prompts), file permissions (0600/0700), the
DNS-rebinding-defense "single resolution reused for the whole push"
behavior, netpolicy refusal propagation, missing-credential/host-key
errors, scratch-directory cleanup (including on early failure), a
password leak-hunt across every captured argv/env, per-server git
identity threading, the git-version gate, soft_ssh_check's
ok/failed-category/skipped outcomes, and (round 9) GIT_SSL_CAINFO
threading: set from SSL_CERT_FILE in HTTP mode, absent when
SSL_CERT_FILE is unset, a pre-existing GIT_SSL_CAINFO respected over
the inference, and SSH mode never touched by any of it. tox -e pep8
and tox -e py3 pass (1745 tests).

  keyscan step already vetted; response shape is unchanged
  ("ok" | "failed: <category>" | "skipped").

Round-9 fix: the next deterministic Zuul failure, one layer deeper
than the round-6/7 ones (Archon's CI diagnosis on 1001734 PS3): the
multi-Gerrit setup, credential verification, and reads all worked --
the first HTTP-mode gerrit_create_change then failed cloning
https://gate-gerrit/a/gate/sandbox/ with git/libcurl rejecting the
fixture certificate ("certificate signer not trusted", using
/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt, git's OWN default bundle).
httpx (this module's own REST clients, and the console door's OIDC
discovery) honors SSL_CERT_FILE natively for its trust store, but
git's own HTTPS transport (libcurl) does not -- it needs
GIT_SSL_CAINFO (env) or http.sslCAInfo (config) to trust anything
beyond its compiled-in default, and _env_for_target (which owns the
git subprocess env construction for HTTP-mode targets) never threaded
SSL_CERT_FILE through to it.

Fixed generically, not as gate-only plumbing: when the gateway
process's own environment carries SSL_CERT_FILE, _env_for_target now
also sets GIT_SSL_CAINFO to that same path for HTTP-mode targets,
unless GIT_SSL_CAINFO is already present in the process env (an
operator who set it explicitly -- deliberately a different trust
store just for git -- wins over the inference). Documented in the
function's own docstring as the general production behavior it is:
an operator pointing the whole gateway at a private-CA Gerrit via
SSL_CERT_FILE now gets git trusting the same store httpx already
does, not just REST calls. Checked DEPLOYMENT.md/README.rst/doc/ for
any existing SSL_CERT_FILE documentation to extend with a one-line
git-follows-it-too note -- none exists (SSL_CERT_FILE is currently
gate-only plumbing, never operator-documented), so no doc section was
invented.

Round-10 fix (Archon, on both 1001707 PS7 and 1001721 PS9, replacing
his prior +1 on this change -- a production-path blocker, not gate
plumbing): create_change's Change-Id stamping relied ENTIRELY on the
commit-msg hook installed by `git review -s`
(workspace.ensure_source_clone / _ensure_source_clone_for_target,
both already best-effort/non-fatal by design). That install can fail
silently: a registered Gerrit whose advertised hook-download URL
differs from the address this module actually reaches it on (the gate
fixture's 127.0.0.1:8083, unreachable from inside the gateway
container, is the concrete case found; any real Gerrit with a
canonical-vs-reachable URL mismatch has the identical shape) leaves
.git/hooks/commit-msg never installed. The old
`git rebase --exec 'git commit --amend --no-edit'` depended wholly on
that hook firing to add anything, so with none installed it was a
pure no-op -- a commit could reach the real Gerrit with NO Change-Id
trailer at all, which Gerrit rejects server-side ("missing Change-Id
in message footer"). Both account types funnel through this one
function, so the old design's vulnerability was shared, not
registered-server-specific.

Fixed with independent, hook-free Change-Id generation plus a
fail-closed invariant check (Archon's own "second option," explicitly
preferred over merely making the hook install more reliable):
_stamp_change_ids_over_range's rebase --exec step now runs a small,
self-contained script (_CHANGE_ID_STAMP_SCRIPT) instead of a bare
`git commit --amend --no-edit`: it still gives a real installed hook
the first chance to fire (free when present, a no-op when it isn't),
then checks HEAD's message directly and, if a Change-Id is still
missing, generates one locally by hashing the same shape of input
Gerrit's own hook hashes (tree + parent + author + committer +
message, fed to `git hash-object -t commit` as a synthetic commit
object) and amends it in -- no hook, no network, dependent on nothing
but the commit's own already-committed content. Commits that already
carry a Change-Id (from a working hook, or because the input already
had one) are left completely untouched, verbatim; exact byte-parity
with the real hook's own message-cleaning rules was deliberately not
attempted -- only the I<40-hex> shape and per-commit uniqueness are
required, and both are guaranteed by construction. A new
_verify_change_ids_over_range, called by create_change right after
stamping and before anything is collected/pushed, is the fail-closed
invariant Archon asked for: every commit about to be pushed must carry
EXACTLY ONE well-formed Change-Id trailer, or a specific internal
PatchError is raised before git-review (and the real Gerrit) ever see
it. It should never actually fire -- stamping guarantees the invariant
on its own -- but turns a hypothetical future regression into an
immediate, actionable error instead of an opaque server-side
rejection.

`git review -s` itself is left in place, unchanged, in
_ensure_source_clone_for_target: it was already best-effort/non-fatal
before this fix and stays that way after it -- the smallest honest
change, since ripping it out would trade a working, harmless call (and
the existing TestEnsureSourceCloneForTargetTempCleanupOnException
regression coverage built around it) for no behavioral gain now that
Change-Id stamping no longer depends on whether it ever succeeds; its
own docstring and log message now say so explicitly. The default
server path (workspace.ensure_source_clone) shares the identical
best-effort hook-install shape and was therefore equally vulnerable
before this fix -- both are covered by the same one fix, in the one
function (_stamp_change_ids_over_range) both create_change flows
already funnel through, with no per-path duplication needed.

tests/gate/check_multi_gerrit_tools.py needed no functional changes:
its create-change assertions read change_numbers/diffstat/file_hashes
and the pushed commit's committer via anonymous REST, never anything
Change-Id-shaped, so nothing there assumed hook-based stamping.

Tests (real git throughout, not mocked calls):
_stamp_change_ids_over_range/_verify_change_ids_over_range exercised
against a repo with NO commit-msg hook installed at all (simulating a
failed/absent `git review -s` hook install): every commit in a
multi-commit stack gets a valid I<40-hex> Change-Id, distinct per
commit; a pre-existing Change-Id (as revise/replace's
_set_head_change_id already guaranteed, and as a create mbox whose tip
was stamped by a working hook would carry) is preserved verbatim, not
regenerated; the same stamp-then-verify sequence run against a real
format-patch mbox applied via git am (mirroring create_change's own
strip -> am -> stamp order) end to end; and the fail-closed verifier
raises PatchError naming the exact wrong count for a commit missing a
trailer and for one carrying two, and stays silent once a stack is
properly stamped. Every new test was confirmed to fail against the
pre-fix hook-only stamping (git commit --amend --no-edit alone) before
being accepted. tox -e pep8 and tox -e py3 pass (1752 tests).

Add UNSYNC operating status for replicas

Docker health checks report database availability but do not show
whether a replica is still synchronized with its source.

Run an optional datastore-specific replication health check from the
existing guest-agent status periodic task. Report UNSYNC when
replication is stopped or the configured lag tolerance is exceeded,
while keeping the database available for instance actions.

For WAL receiver replication, check the source connection first and
only use the last replay timestamp while disconnected. Treat a missing
timestamp as UNSYNC, covering replicas that can no longer replay the
required WAL after rebuild.

revisions.message:
kernel: enable in-tree Intel FPGA (DFL/OPAE) support

Enable the in-tree Device Feature List (DFL) stack in both kernel-rt and
kernel-std configs so that Intel FPGA / OPAE cards (e.g. Intel PAC N3000)
are supported by the mainline drivers, without relying on the
out-of-tree opae-intel-fpga-driver DKMS package.

The OOT OPAE 2.0.1 driver mapped onto the upstream DFL framework
(drivers/fpga/dfl*) plus the MAX10 BMC, SPI, MTD and regmap pieces it
depends on. Enable the full chain as modules:

- FPGA core: FPGA, FPGA_BRIDGE, FPGA_REGION and the DFL bus
  (FPGA_DFL, FPGA_DFL_FME{,_MGR,_BRIDGE,_REGION}, FPGA_DFL_AFU,
  FPGA_DFL_PCI, FPGA_DFL_NIOS_INTEL_PAC_N3000, FPGA_M10_BMC_SEC_UPDATE)
  plus the Altera/Xilinx/Lattice/Microchip managers and bridges.
- MAX10 BMC: MFD_INTEL_M10_BMC_CORE/_SPI/_PMCI and
  SENSORS_INTEL_M10_BMC_HWMON.
- Buses/flash used by the above: REGMAP_SPI_AVMM, SPI_MEM,
  SPI_ALTERA{,_CORE,_DFL}, SPI_INTEL{,_PCI,_PLATFORM}, MTD_SPI_NOR.

The config change is identical for kernel-rt and kernel-std to keep both
flavours aligned. New collateral symbols surfaced by enabling the above
(SERIAL_8250_DFL, PTP_DFL_TOD, SPI_ZYNQMP_GQSPI, SPI_AMD) are left at
their disabled defaults.

In addition, backport the OPAE image_load sysfs interface that mainline
does not carry:

- fpga/0001-fpga-m10bmc-sec-add-image_load-sysfs-for-N3000-and-D.patch:
  the mainline MAX10 BMC secure-update driver exposes only the
  firmware-upload ABI and lacks the control/available_images and
  control/image_load attributes OPAE userspace uses to trigger an RSU
  or retimer firmware reload. Add the N3000 and D5005 subset (bmc_user,
  bmc_factory, and retimer_fw for N3000), ported from linux-dfl commits
  e1b885714f68 and 604ad4f48cee, along with the M10BMC_PKVL_POLL_CTRL
  register definitions in intel-m10-bmc.h needed by the retimer path.
  N6000/PMCI/SDM handlers are intentionally left out; the N6000 ops keep
  .image_load = NULL so the control/ group stays hidden for them.

The patch is applied to both kernel-rt and kernel-std.

Verification:
- Build kernel and out of tree modules success for rt and std.
- Build iso success for rt and std.
- Install success onto a lab with std kernel, and can switch to rt.
- Boot up successfully in the lab; DFL/FPGA modules load and the
  FPGA devices enumerate.
- On Intel PAC N3000, control/available_images reports
  "bmc_factory bmc_user retimer_fw" and image_load accepts a valid name.
- The sanity testing was run and the test results PASS.

kernel: add OPAE SDK userspace package for Debian trixie

Add a new userspace package, userspace/opae-sdk, that builds the Intel
OPAE SDK 2.14.0-3 for the Debian trixie layer. This is the userspace
companion to the in-tree Intel FPGA (DFL/OPAE) kernel enablement: it
provides the OPAE runtime, the development files and the extra FPGA
tools used to manage Intel FPGA / OPAE cards (e.g. Intel PAC N3000).

The source is the upstream release tarball
(https://github.com/OFS/opae-sdk/archive/refs/tags/2.14.0-3.zip). As it
is a .zip whose top-level directory is opae-sdk-2.14.0-3, a dl_hook
unzips it and renames the tree to <debname>-<debver> (opae-2.14.0-3),
mirroring the existing kernel-modules/intel-opae-fpga zip handling.

The Debian packaging under debian/trixie/deb_folder is derived from the
upstream packaging/opae/deb tree and adapted for the trixie toolchain:

- control: Maintainer switched to StarlingX, debhelper-compat (= 13),
  and the Build-Depends completed for an out-of-the-box build:
  pkg-config, pybind11-dev, libcli11-dev, libspdlog-dev and libnuma-dev
  (OPAE would otherwise FetchContent these, which debhelper disables),
  python3-jsonschema and python3-yaml (needed by the build-time
  ofs_parse.py generator), plus python3-pip/setuptools/wheel for the
  OPAE_BUILD_PYTHON_DIST stage.
- rules: set DEB_BUILD_OPTIONS=noddebs; reference the out-of-tree cmake
  build dir as obj-$(DEB_HOST_GNU_TYPE) instead of a hardcoded arch;
  pip-install the python dist artifacts with --break-system-packages and
  DEB_PYTHON_INSTALL_LAYOUT=deb_system so they land under /usr and
  dist-packages (PEP 668 / trixie). OPAE's cmake also stages those
  python packages under /usr/local, so the duplicate /usr/local tree is
  removed before packaging.
- opae-devel.install: add the cmake package-config exports
  (usr/lib/opae-2.14.0/*.cmake and modules/*.cmake) and the top-level
  usr/include/opae/cxx/core.h header, and resolve the @VERSION@
  placeholder in opae-devel.dirs to 2.14.0.

The package is registered for the trixie std build in
debian_trixie_pkg_dirs_std, and the three resulting binary packages
(opae, opae-devel, opae-extra-tools) are added to
debian_trixie_iso_image_std.inc.

Test Plan:
Pass: downloader - dl_hook unzips and renames to opae-2.14.0-3
Pass: build opae, opae-devel and opae-extra-tools (Debian trixie,
      debian:13, amd64)
Pass: dpkg-deb metadata sane - versions 2.14.0-3, opae-devel depends
      opae (= 2.14.0-3), opae-extra-tools depends opae + opae-devel,
      shlib dependencies auto-resolved
Pass: no dh_missing failures - runtime libraries/binaries, headers and
      FPGA tools present in the expected packages

revisions.message:
Adapt served map fragments to layer specs

Phase 6 of the API repo's doc/plans/mapstyle-architecture.md begins:
clients stop building map style, servers serve it. The API now
composes each user's track sources and layers from the grouping
constants and their tile files, so this app's paint, layout and base
filter builders have a replacement waiting for them.

This change is the pure addition that makes the flip possible, not
the flip itself. api.ts learns the two fragment endpoints, reusing
the grouping conversion the grouping endpoints already apply rather
than growing a second answer to what shape a grouping is. The new
map/fragment-adapter.ts reshapes a served document into the same
TileSourceLayerSpec/TrackLayerSpec values WanderTracksMap.syncTracks
and the editor's applier consume today, so the follow-up host change
is a swap of one builder for another and nothing else moves.

What stays client-side is only what is dynamic: which groupings are
switched on, and whose vehicles' tracks are wanted. The vehicle
clause of buildGroupingFilter is ported over verbatim, including the
never-true expression that means "nothing selected draws nothing",
and composed onto the served base filter rather than into it - the
expression is the API's to own now.

The tests drive the adapter with a document generated by running the
API's own mapfragments.py over two tile files and the fourteen
groupings, so what they pin is the contract rather than a
restatement of it. The bundled tile file's id is a UUID on purpose:
layer ids are track-{tilefile}-{grouping} and the tile file half
contains hyphens, so the split matches the served grouping ids
instead of guessing at separators.

subject: Adapt served map fragments to layer specs

revisions.message:
Fail CI when vendored basemaps drift

app/src/main/assets/basemaps holds copies of the API repo's
wandertracks/mapstyles -- the same style JSON the API serves at
/api/v1/styles/<basemap>.json, carried in the APK so a device that
cannot reach the API renders the same map it would have gotten
online. They were hand-synced, and BasemapStyleProvider's own
comment said so. Hand-synced cross-repo copies are precisely the
drift the mapstyle-centralization effort exists to kill: the
failure mode is silent, only visible on a phone that happens to be
offline, and arbitrarily long after the API-side edit that caused
it.

So add wandertracks-android-basemap-parity, running the assets
against the API repo's originals in a required-projects checkout.
It is not a child of wandertracks-android-base -- the check is a
python3 stdlib script over parsed JSON, needing neither the SDK nor
Gradle -- and it carries no files matcher, because a drift detector
that only runs when someone touched the assets cannot catch the
change that forgot to. required-projects also makes Depends-On work
across the repos, so a style edit upstream and the asset refresh
here gate together.

Parity is asserted on the parsed JSON rather than the bytes,
because exactly two differences are legitimate. Serialization: the
API repo's files are pretty-printed for human review, the assets
are compact because the phone parses them rather than reading them.
Key order: nothing on either side depends on it. Everything else
fails, including the {{ESRI_API_TOKEN}} placeholder, which is the
on-disk form on both sides -- the API substitutes it at serve time
and BasemapStyleProvider at load time, so a real token appearing in
either tree is drift and comparing the placeholder text verbatim is
what catches it.

All five styles are in sync today; this pins that. The script takes
the two directories as arguments and defaults to the side-by-side
checkout layout, so it runs locally as well as in the job, and it
exits non-zero rather than skipping when it cannot find one side --
a parity check that passes when it looked at nothing is worse than
no parity check.

revisions.message:
Retire the deprecated grouping endpoints

Track styling is derived once, server-side, and shipped to clients as
finished MapLibre sources and layers by the map-fragments endpoints.
The grouping endpoints existed only to feed the client-side layer
builders that composed those specs themselves: the web's builders are
gone, the styling editor page is gone, and Android never called them.
The same constants still reach clients, inside the fragments payload.

Removed: GET /api/v1/trackgroupings (namespace and module) and
GET /api/v1/public/u/{slug}/groupings with its response model.

The config endpoint's esri_api_token goes with them for the same
reason: it parameterized client-built basemap styles, and the API now
renders those styles itself, substituting the token when it serves
/api/v1/styles/<basemap>.json. That substitution keeps the default
token, which moves to styles.py alongside its only remaining reader;
WANDERTRACKS_ESRI_API_TOKEN still overrides it.

The unit test for the retired routes becomes an assertion that they
are absent from the URL map, so a re-registration is caught.
